Forcepoint KB: 'Handling QUIC and HTTP/3 traffic with Forcepoint Web Security Content Gateway' (Article ID: 000014312). Validate QUIC bypass by capturing traffic with Wireshark on an external interface to confirm that QUIC connections are being blocked and browsers are falling back to HTTPS.

questions.text: Are roaming users correctly redirected to hybrid - proxy services?
questions.description: Roaming users (employees working outside the corporate network) who are not correctly redirected to Forcepoint Web Security hybrid cloud proxy services are completely unfiltered and unprotected. This is one of the most common and impactful security gaps in enterprise web security deployments, particularly for organisations with significant remote or mobile workforces.
questions.remediation:
Verify that the Forcepoint Web Security endpoint agent (F1E/Web Security Endpoint) is deployed on all roaming user devices and that it is configured to redirect traffic to the correct hybrid proxy endpoints when off-network. Confirm that PAC file-based roaming redirection or agent-based redirection is functioning by testing from a device outside the corporate network perimeter.

Forcepoint KB: 'Configuring hybrid proxy redirection for roaming users with Forcepoint Web Security' (Article ID: 000012673). Check endpoint agent status in TRITON Manager > Web > Settings > Hybrid Configuration and verify that registered endpoints are appearing in the hybrid portal dashboard.

questions.text: Are uncategorized URLs being reviewed regularly?
questions.description: Uncategorized URLs represent a grey area in web filtering policy — they are URLs that the Forcepoint Master Database has not classified. Without a defined and enforced policy for uncategorized URLs, they may be permitted by default, creating a bypass vector for malicious or policy-violating content hosted on newly registered or obscure domains.
questions.remediation:
Define an explicit policy action for uncategorized URLs (recommend: Block or Confirm, not Allow) in all user-facing policies in TRITON Manager. Enable the Uncategorized URL report in TRITON Manager > Reports to review frequently accessed uncategorized URLs. Submit frequently accessed legitimate uncategorized URLs to Forcepoint for database classification using the Threat Intelligence Exchange (TIE) portal.

Forcepoint KB: 'Managing uncategorized URL traffic in Forcepoint Web Security' (Article ID: 000010891). Submit URLs for classification at https://csi.forcepoint.com. Review uncategorized traffic weekly and escalate patterns of suspicious uncategorized domains for threat investigation.

questions.text: Are anonymizers and proxy avoidance tools blocked?
questions.description: Anonymizers, VPN clients, TOR exit nodes, and proxy avoidance tools are specifically designed to circumvent web filtering. If not blocked, users can tunnel all of their traffic through these services, completely bypassing Forcepoint Web Security policy enforcement, DLP scanning, and logging. This represents a complete nullification of the web security investment.
questions.remediation:
Confirm that the 'Proxy Avoidance' and 'Anonymous Proxies' categories are set to Block in all user-facing policies. Enable blocking of TOR exit node IPs using the Forcepoint Security Labs threat feed. Review outbound traffic to non-standard ports (e.g., UDP/9001, TCP/9001 for TOR) at the firewall level. Consider blocking DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) resolvers that can be used to circumvent DNS-based categorisation.

Forcepoint KB: 'Blocking proxy avoidance and anonymizer tools in Forcepoint Web Security' (Article ID: 000011345). Additionally, block DoH endpoints (1.1.1.1:443, 8.8.8.8:443 on application layer) and force all DNS through corporate resolvers to prevent DNS-based category lookup bypass.

questions.text: Are risky SaaS applications monitored or blocked?
questions.description: Unsanctioned or high-risk SaaS applications (file sharing services, personal email, messaging platforms, AI tools with data upload capabilities) can be used intentionally or unintentionally to exfiltrate sensitive data, bypass corporate communication controls, or introduce malware. Without visibility and control, shadow IT SaaS usage expands unchecked.
questions.remediation:
Use Forcepoint Web Security application controls to identify and categorise SaaS applications in use across the organisation. Define policies to block or restrict high-risk applications (personal file sharing, uncategorised cloud storage) and apply read-only or upload-limited policies to tolerated-but-monitored applications. Integrate with Forcepoint CASB for deeper in-session visibility into sanctioned cloud app activity.

Forcepoint KB: 'Configuring application controls for SaaS applications in Forcepoint Web Security' (Article ID: 000013672). Review Application Usage reports in TRITON Manager > Reports > Web > Applications to identify the SaaS application footprint in the organisation.

questions.text: Are endpoint agents online and reporting correctly?
questions.description: Endpoint agents (Forcepoint Web Security Endpoint / F1E) that are offline, unregistered, or reporting errors indicate gaps in web protection coverage for those devices. Users on unprotected endpoints can browse without filtering, logging, or DLP inspection, creating both security and compliance gaps.
questions.remediation:
Review endpoint agent status in TRITON Manager > Web > Settings > Hybrid Configuration > Endpoints. Identify endpoints that have not reported within the expected check-in interval and investigate the cause (device offline, agent crash, network connectivity issues, or software conflict). Re-push the endpoint agent via management tooling (Intune, SCCM, JAMF) to devices with missing or outdated agents.

Forcepoint KB: 'Troubleshooting Forcepoint Web Security Endpoint agent registration and reporting issues' (Article ID: 000013456). Review endpoint agent logs on the client device at %ProgramData%\Websense\Web Security Endpoint\Logs for connectivity and registration errors.

questions.description: Without tamper protection, users with local administrator rights can disable, uninstall, or bypass the Forcepoint Web Security endpoint agent. This is a critical control failure, as technically capable users or malware with elevated privileges can trivially remove the endpoint filtering layer.
questions.remediation:
Enable tamper protection features within the Forcepoint Web Security Endpoint policy configuration. Configure the agent to require an administrative password for uninstallation or configuration changes. Combine with OS-level controls (application control, software restriction policies) to prevent agent binary modification. Monitor for endpoint agent status changes in the TRITON management console as an indicator of tampering attempts.

Forcepoint KB: 'Enabling and verifying endpoint agent tamper protection in Forcepoint Web Security' (Article ID: 000013789). Review agent policy settings in TRITON Manager > Web > Settings > Hybrid Configuration > Endpoint Policy and test protection by attempting agent uninstallation from a test endpoint without the correct credentials.

questions.text: Is Remote Browser Isolation (RBI) solution deployed and actively used?
questions.description: Without Remote Browser Isolation, users browsing risky or uncategorized websites execute web content locally in their browser, exposing endpoints to drive-by download attacks, malicious scripts, and browser exploits. RBI eliminates this risk by executing all web rendering in an isolated cloud environment and streaming only a safe pixel representation or sanitized DOM to the user.
questions.remediation:
Verify that Forcepoint RBI (integrated with Forcepoint Web Security via redirect policies) is licensed, configured, and actively receiving traffic for designated risk categories (e.g., Uncategorized, Potentially Harmful, User-defined watch list). Review RBI session counts and error rates in the RBI management portal. Confirm that the RBI redirect URL is correctly configured in Content Gateway redirect policies and test RBI activation from a client device.

Forcepoint KB: 'Integrating Forcepoint RBI with Forcepoint Web Security for category-based isolation' (Article ID: 000014023). Check RBI integration configuration in Content Gateway Manager > Configure > Redirect Policies and verify tenant configuration in the Forcepoint RBI administration portal.

questions.text: Are users communicating with potentially malicious or suspicious websites observed on the dashboard?
questions.description: Active communication with malicious or suspicious websites observed in the Forcepoint Web Security dashboard indicates that one or more endpoints may be compromised, infected with malware, or that users are intentionally accessing harmful content. C2 communication, botnet check-ins, and phishing site access are common indicators observed in this context.
questions.remediation:
Immediately investigate the specific user accounts and endpoint devices generating traffic to malicious destinations. Isolate affected endpoints for forensic analysis. Review the full session history for affected users in TRITON Manager Investigative Reports to identify the scope of the communication. Escalate findings to the incident response team. Ensure that the destination URLs/IPs are added to a custom block list if not already categorised.

Forcepoint KB: 'Investigating malicious website access alerts in Forcepoint Web Security' — refer to the TRITON Manager > Reports > Real-Time Monitor and Investigative Reports for drill-down on suspicious activity. Cross-reference identified malicious IPs/domains with the Forcepoint CSI (Cloud Security Intelligence) portal at https://csi.forcepoint.com for threat intelligence context.

questions.text: Is Log Server successfully writing logs to the SQL database?
questions.description: Log Server may fail to write logs into the SQL database due to connectivity, ETL, ODBC/BCP, permission, or disk-related issues. This can result in missing reports, incomplete investigations, and loss of visibility within the Forcepoint environment.
questions.remediation:
Verify SQL connectivity, review Log Server status, validate ODBC/BCP configuration, ensure SQL Agent jobs are operational, and confirm sufficient disk space is available on both Log Server and SQL Server systems.

Forcepoint KB: 'Troubleshooting Log Server database write failures in Forcepoint Web Security' (Article ID: 000010567). Review Log Server service status in Windows Services and check %ProgramFiles%\Websense\Web Security\logs\LogServer.log for SQL connection or write errors. Validate that the SQL Server Agent service is running and that Forcepoint ETL jobs are enabled under SQL Server Agent > Jobs.

questions.text: Are SQL ETL jobs operating successfully without buffer table errors?
questions.description: SQL ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) jobs are responsible for moving log data from buffer tables into the main reporting partitions in the Forcepoint log database. ETL job failures or errors result in buffer table overflow, which causes Log Server to halt new log writes, creating gaps in the audit trail and reporting data.
questions.remediation:
Check SQL Server Agent job history for Forcepoint ETL jobs and identify any failed or long-running steps. Review the buffer table row counts in the wslogdb70 database — high row counts in the Buffer table indicate ETL backlog. Investigate root causes such as SQL Server resource constraints, long-running queries, or permission issues. Restart ETL jobs manually if they have stalled.

Forcepoint KB: 'SQL ETL job failures and buffer table overflow in Forcepoint Web Security Log Database' (Article ID: 000011234). Query buffer table health: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM wslogdb70..Internet_Detail_Buffer. Engage Forcepoint Technical Support if ETL jobs cannot be restored to normal operation.

questions.text: Are database partitions being created and maintained successfully?
questions.description: The Forcepoint log database uses a monthly partition scheme to organise web access logs and enable efficient reporting. If partition creation fails (due to insufficient disk space, SQL permissions, or maintenance job failures), new log data cannot be inserted into the database, causing Log Server failures and loss of reporting data from the point of partition creation failure.
questions.remediation:
Verify that the monthly partition creation SQL Agent job has run successfully for the current month. Check SQL Server Management Studio > wslogdb70 > Tables for the existence of the current month's Internet_Detail_YYYYMM table. If the partition is missing, run the partition creation stored procedure manually or trigger the SQL Agent job. Investigate and resolve any disk space or permission issues that may have caused the failure.

Forcepoint KB: 'Database partition creation failures in Forcepoint Web Security Log Database' (Article ID: 000011678). Confirm current partition exists: SELECT name FROM sys.tables WHERE name LIKE 'Internet_Detail_%' ORDER BY name DESC. Contact Forcepoint Support if the partition creation procedure fails with SQL errors.

questions.text: Can the Log Server establish stable communication with the SQL Server?
questions.description: Log Server relies on a stable TCP connection to the SQL Server instance hosting the Forcepoint log database. Connectivity interruptions — caused by network instability, SQL Server restarts, firewall rule changes, or SQL authentication failures — result in Log Server queuing and eventually dropping log events, creating gaps in the audit trail.
questions.remediation:
Test SQL Server connectivity from the Log Server host using SQLCMD or ODBC Data Source Administrator (odbcad32.exe). Verify that TCP port 1433 (or the custom SQL port if configured) is open between the Log Server and SQL Server hosts. Confirm that the SQL service account credentials used by Log Server have not expired. Check Windows Event Viewer on the Log Server host for ODBC/SQL connectivity error events.

Forcepoint KB: 'Troubleshooting Log Server to SQL Server connectivity in Forcepoint Web Security' (Article ID: 000010943). Review LogServer.log at %ProgramFiles%\Websense\Web Security\logs\ for SQL connection error messages and timestamps to correlate with any known network or SQL maintenance events.

questions.text: Are email gateway connectors properly configured?
questions.description: Misconfigured email gateway connectors — incorrect smart host settings, wrong relay source IPs, or missing authentication — can cause inbound or outbound email delivery failures, routing loops, or complete bypass of the security gateway. Connector misconfiguration is a leading cause of email delivery incidents and security gaps.
questions.remediation:
Review all inbound and outbound connector configurations in the Forcepoint Email Security management console. Verify that the inbound connector accepts email for all expected domains and that TLS settings match the requirements of sending mail servers. Confirm that the outbound connector routes through the gateway correctly and that SPF records reflect the gateway's sending IP addresses.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint Email Security Administrator Guide > Mail Flow Configuration. Engage TAC for complex multi-gateway or hybrid connector configuration issues.

questions.text: Is MX record pointing to email gateway?
questions.description: If the MX record does not point to the Forcepoint Email Security gateway, inbound email is delivered directly to the mail server, bypassing all anti-spam, anti-malware, DLP, and quarantine controls. DNS misconfiguration of the MX record is a catastrophic security gap that can persist for extended periods without detection.
questions.remediation:
Verify the MX record for all protected domains using an external DNS lookup tool (MXToolbox, dig). Confirm that the MX record resolves to the IP address of the Forcepoint Email Security gateway, not directly to the Exchange/Microsoft 365 server. If Microsoft 365 is used, verify that the Exchange Online connector restricts inbound email to arrive only from Forcepoint gateway IP ranges.

Forcepoint KB: 'Verifying MX record configuration for Forcepoint Email Security' — refer to the Forcepoint Email Security Deployment Guide.

questions.description: Incorrect relay settings on the email gateway can allow the system to be used as an open relay, causing the gateway's IP to be blacklisted by RBL providers and all outbound email to be rejected by recipient mail servers. An open relay is also exploitable by spammers for high-volume abuse.
questions.remediation:
In the Forcepoint Email Security console, verify that relay settings accept inbound email only for explicitly defined protected domains and relay outbound email only from authenticated or IP-whitelisted internal mail servers. Test relay configuration from an external IP address to confirm rejection of relay attempts for non-protected domains.

Forcepoint KB: 'Configuring relay settings and preventing open relay in Forcepoint Email Security' — refer to the Administrator Guide > Mail Routing and Relay. Periodically check the gateway's sending IP against common RBL lists (MXToolbox, Spamhaus).

questions.text: Is TLS encryption enabled for email transport?
questions.description: Email transmitted without TLS encryption is vulnerable to interception and man-in-the-middle attacks during transit between mail servers. Regulatory frameworks (GDPR, PCI-DSS, HIPAA) and organisational security policies typically require encryption in transit for email containing sensitive information.
questions.remediation:
Enable opportunistic TLS (STARTTLS) for all inbound and outbound email connections in the Forcepoint Email Security gateway. For high-sensitivity communications with specific partners, configure enforced TLS. Verify TLS negotiation success by reviewing mail logs and using external testing tools (CheckTLS.com). Set minimum TLS version to TLS 1.2.

Forcepoint KB: 'Configuring TLS encryption for email transport in Forcepoint Email Security' — refer to the Administrator Guide > TLS Configuration.

questions.description: If accepted domains are not correctly configured in the email gateway, email for legitimate company domains may be rejected with 'user unknown' errors, causing delivery failures for business-critical communications. Conversely, if too many domains are accepted, the gateway may inadvertently relay spam.
questions.remediation:
Review the accepted domain list in the Forcepoint Email Security console and verify that it includes all domains for which the gateway should accept inbound email. Verify against the organisation's authoritative list of active email domains including any subsidiary or legacy domains. Remove any domains that are no longer in use.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint Email Security Administrator Guide > Domain Configuration.

questions.description: Email routing failures — where messages are accepted by the gateway but not delivered to the internal mail server, or where outbound messages are routed incorrectly — can result in lost email, delivery delays, or messages being delivered to the wrong recipient system. Routing misconfigurations are often caused by internal mail server IP/hostname changes not reflected in the gateway.
questions.remediation:
Trace the routing path of a test email through the Forcepoint Email Security gateway from inbound acceptance to delivery to the internal mail server. Review the mail routing configuration and verify that smart host/relay settings point to the correct internal mail server addresses. Review gateway mail logs for routing errors (4xx/5xx SMTP response codes).

Forcepoint KB: 'Troubleshooting email routing in Forcepoint Email Security' — refer to the Administrator Guide > Mail Routing.

questions.text: Are SPF, DKIM, and DMARC configured?
questions.description: Without correctly configured SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records, the organisation's email domain is vulnerable to spoofing and phishing attacks where attackers send email impersonating the company's domain to external recipients. Major email providers (Google, Microsoft) increasingly require DMARC for reliable email delivery.
questions.remediation:
Verify the SPF record for all sending domains includes all IP addresses used by the Forcepoint Email Security gateway. Ensure DKIM signing is enabled in the gateway for outbound email and that the DKIM public key is published in DNS. Configure DMARC with at minimum a 'p=quarantine' policy and configure DMARC aggregate reporting to a monitored mailbox.

Forcepoint KB: 'Configuring DKIM signing in Forcepoint Email Security' — refer to the Administrator Guide > Email Authentication.

questions.text: Is SSL inspection enabled and working?
questions.description: The majority of web traffic is encrypted via HTTPS. Without SSL inspection, the proxy cannot scan content, enforce policies on URLs within HTTPS sessions, detect malware in encrypted downloads, or prevent data exfiltration over encrypted channels. Attackers routinely use HTTPS to evade detection.
questions.remediation:
Confirm that SSL Manager is enabled in Content Gateway and that the SSL CA certificate is deployed to all endpoints via GPO or MDM. Verify that decryption policies are appropriately configured with bypass rules only for genuinely required destinations (e.g., banking, healthcare). Monitor SSL inspection throughput and error rates in Content Gateway Manager.

Forcepoint KB: 'SSL Manager configuration and troubleshooting in Content Gateway' (Article ID: 000010892). Check Content Gateway Manager > Configure > SSL > SSL Manager for current inspection status and certificate deployment.

questions.description: Spam thresholds that are set too permissively allow spam to reach user inboxes, while overly aggressive thresholds cause legitimate email to be quarantined, impacting business communications. Threshold configuration requires ongoing tuning based on the organisation's user population, communication patterns, and threat landscape.
questions.remediation:
Review spam score threshold settings in the Forcepoint Email Security console for the spam, suspected spam, and bulk email categories. Compare configured thresholds against Forcepoint's recommended values. Analyse quarantine false positive rates by reviewing user quarantine release requests. Adjust thresholds in small increments and monitor impact.

Forcepoint KB: 'Spam threshold configuration and tuning guide for Forcepoint Email Security' — refer to the Administrator Guide > Anti-Spam Thresholds.

questions.description: RBL checking allows the email gateway to reject connection attempts from known spam-sending IP addresses at the SMTP connection stage, before any message content is processed. Without RBL enabled, the gateway processes significantly more spam messages, increasing CPU load and the risk of spam reaching users through content filter gaps.
questions.remediation:
Enable RBL lookups in the Forcepoint Email Security anti-spam configuration. Configure at minimum the Spamhaus ZEN and Barracuda RBL feeds. Verify that DNS is configured to resolve RBL lookup queries without timeouts. Monitor RBL rejection rates in the gateway logs to confirm that RBL is actively filtering connections.

Forcepoint KB: 'Configuring RBL checking in Forcepoint Email Security' — refer to the Administrator Guide > Connection-level Spam Controls.

questions.description: Sender reputation checks evaluate the sending IP's history against threat intelligence databases. Without reputation-based filtering, email from IP addresses with established spam-sending histories is processed without this signal, reducing detection rates for high-volume spam and phishing campaigns.
questions.remediation:
Verify that sender reputation checking is enabled in the Forcepoint Email Security anti-spam configuration. Confirm that the Forcepoint ThreatSeeker Intelligence feed is active and that reputation data is current. Review sender reputation block rates in the reporting dashboard to confirm the feature is contributing to spam detection.

Forcepoint KB: 'Sender reputation configuration in Forcepoint Email Security' — refer to the Administrator Guide > Reputation Services.

questions.description: Greylisting (temporarily deferring email from unknown senders) is an effective technique for reducing spam from botnet-controlled IP addresses, as botnet nodes typically do not retry failed deliveries. However, greylisting introduces delivery delays for first-time senders that may be unacceptable for time-sensitive business communications.
questions.remediation:
Evaluate whether greylisting is appropriate for the organisation's email patterns. If implemented, configure greylisting with a short deferral period (5-15 minutes). Whitelist trusted sender IP ranges (major cloud providers, business partners) to avoid greylisting delays for known-good sources. Monitor greylisting impact through delivery time metrics.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint Email Security Administrator Guide > Anti-Spam Options for greylisting configuration.

questions.description: Without monitoring anti-spam false positive rates, the operations team cannot determine whether legitimate business emails are being incorrectly quarantined. Unmonitored false positives can cause missed business communications, strained partner relationships, and escalating help desk volumes from users reporting missing email.
questions.remediation:
Configure scheduled false positive analysis reports in the Forcepoint Email Security reporting console. Review the quarantine release report to identify patterns of released messages that may indicate systematic false positive generation. Create sender whitelists for legitimate sources generating false positives. Set a target false positive rate of <0.1% and track it monthly.

Forcepoint KB: 'Managing anti-spam false positives in Forcepoint Email Security' — refer to the Administrator Guide > Quarantine Management.

questions.text: Is spam signature database updated regularly?
questions.description: Spam signature databases that are not regularly updated fail to detect the latest spam campaigns and phishing templates. Spam detection relies heavily on pattern matching against current spam signatures; a stale database is functionally equivalent to partially disabled spam filtering for new campaigns.
questions.remediation:
Verify that the Forcepoint Email Security spam signature database is configured for automatic updates and confirm the last successful update timestamp in the system console. Verify outbound connectivity from the gateway to Forcepoint update servers on port 443. Check for update errors in the system logs.

Forcepoint KB: 'Troubleshooting spam signature database update failures in Forcepoint Email Security' — refer to the Administrator Guide > System Updates.

questions.description: Outdated malware detection engine signatures reduce the gateway's ability to detect newly deployed malware variants, ransomware, and weaponised documents. Modern malware is specifically crafted to evade detection by static signatures, making frequent signature updates essential. A gap of even 24 hours in signature currency can expose the organisation to current attack campaigns.
questions.remediation:
Verify that all malware detection engines in the Forcepoint Email Security gateway are configured for automatic signature updates and confirm the last update timestamp. For deployments using multiple detection engines, verify updates for each engine independently. Confirm outbound connectivity to each engine's update servers.

Forcepoint KB: 'Configuring automatic malware signature updates in Forcepoint Email Security' — refer to the Administrator Guide > Anti-Malware Configuration.

questions.description: Without attachment scanning, malicious files (ransomware executables, macro-enabled Office documents, weaponised PDFs, ZIP-packed malware) pass through the gateway undetected and are delivered directly to user mailboxes. Email is the primary vector for malware delivery in modern enterprise environments.
questions.remediation:
Verify that attachment scanning is enabled in the Forcepoint Email Security anti-malware configuration. Confirm that scanning is applied to all relevant file types including executables, Office documents, PDFs, scripts, and archive formats. Verify that attachment scanning is active for both inbound and outbound email.

Forcepoint KB: 'Configuring attachment scanning in Forcepoint Email Security' — refer to the Administrator Guide > Anti-Malware > Attachment Scanning. Verify that maximum file size limits for scanning are not set too low, causing large attachments to bypass scanning.

questions.description: High-risk file types that are rarely used for legitimate business purposes (double-extension files, executable files, script files, ISO images) pose a significant malware delivery risk if not blocked at the gateway. Attackers use these file types specifically because they are commonly overlooked by email security controls.
questions.remediation:
Configure a file type blocking policy to block high-risk extensions including: .exe, .bat, .cmd, .ps1, .vbs, .js, .jse, .wsf, .hta, .scr, .pif, .iso, .img, and double-extension files. Apply blocks for both inbound and outbound email. Provide a business exception process for cases where legitimate use of these file types is required.

Forcepoint KB: 'Configuring dangerous file type blocking in Forcepoint Email Security' — refer to the Administrator Guide > Content Filtering > File Types.

questions.text: Is sandboxing enabled for suspicious files?
questions.description: Static file scanning cannot detect sophisticated malware that only reveals malicious behaviour during execution in a sandbox environment. Without sandboxing for suspicious email attachments, zero-day malware, polymorphic threats, and evasive payloads that pass static signature checks can be delivered to users.
questions.remediation:
Enable sandbox analysis for suspicious email attachments in the Forcepoint Email Security configuration. For Forcepoint-native deployments, integrate with Forcepoint Advanced Malware Detection (AMD). Verify that the sandbox is receiving files for detonation and generating verdicts. Configure policy actions based on sandbox verdicts (block malicious, hold suspicious for verdict).

Forcepoint KB: 'Configuring Advanced Malware Detection (AMD) sandboxing for email in Forcepoint Email Security' — refer to the Forcepoint AMD Integration Guide. Confirm AMD licensing is current and detonation capacity is sufficient for the email volume.

questions.description: Archive files (ZIP, RAR, 7z, GZ) are frequently used to package malware payloads, bypassing file type blocking rules that check only the outer file extension. Without recursive archive scanning, multi-layer compressed malware (e.g., a ZIP containing a ZIP containing an .exe) can evade detection.
questions.remediation:
Verify that archive file scanning is enabled in the Forcepoint Email Security anti-malware configuration with recursive scanning enabled. Set a maximum recursion depth of at least 5 levels. Configure password-protected archive handling — typically block delivery since password-protected archives cannot be scanned.

Forcepoint KB: 'Configuring archive scanning in Forcepoint Email Security' — refer to the Administrator Guide > Anti-Malware > Archive Handling.

questions.text: Is URL rewriting for click-time protection enabled?
questions.description: URL-based attacks increasingly use time-of-click weaponisation, where URLs in email are benign at delivery time but redirect to malicious content after the message is scanned. Without URL rewriting and click-time protection, users who click links in older emails are not protected after the URL has been weaponised.
questions.remediation:
Enable URL rewriting in the Forcepoint Email Security gateway for all inbound email links. Configure click-time URL analysis to re-evaluate link destinations when users click. Verify that the URL rewriting service is reachable from user endpoints. Configure policy actions for malicious click-time verdicts (block page, user warning, or block).

Forcepoint KB: 'Configuring URL click-time protection in Forcepoint Email Security' — refer to the Administrator Guide > URL Protection. Verify that URL rewriting does not break legitimate links by testing a sample of business communications.

questions.description: Without monitoring malware detection rates, there is no visibility into whether the anti-malware controls are functioning effectively or whether detection rates are declining, possibly indicating evasion of the deployed engines. Trending detection rate data is essential for justifying security investment and identifying when additional controls are needed.
questions.remediation:
Configure scheduled malware detection rate reports in the Forcepoint Email Security reporting dashboard. Track total malicious attachments detected, malware types encountered, and detection engine source over time. Compare detection rates month-over-month. Submit undetected malware samples to Forcepoint Threat Intelligence for engine improvement.

Forcepoint KB: 'Email security reporting in Forcepoint Email Security' — refer to the Reporting Guide for anti-malware detection metrics.

questions.text: Is DLP scanning enabled for outbound email?
questions.description: Without DLP scanning for outbound email, sensitive data (PII, financial information, intellectual property, health records) can be exfiltrated by insiders or inadvertently sent to unauthorised recipients via email. Email is the most common channel for data loss in enterprise environments. Regulatory frameworks (GDPR, PCI-DSS, HIPAA) require controls on sensitive data transmission.
questions.remediation:
Verify that DLP scanning is enabled for outbound email in the Forcepoint Email Security configuration. Confirm that DLP policies are applied to the outbound mail flow rule. Test DLP detection by sending a test email containing synthetic sensitive data (e.g., test PAN, synthetic NHS/TC number) and verifying that it triggers the configured action.

Forcepoint KB: 'Configuring DLP scanning for outbound email in Forcepoint Email Security' — refer to the Forcepoint DLP Integration Guide for Email Security.

questions.text: Are DLP policies aligned with organizational policy?
questions.description: DLP policies that do not align with the organisation's data classification policy or regulatory requirements will either generate excessive false positives (disrupting legitimate communications) or miss genuine data loss events. Policy misalignment is a common cause of DLP programme failure and user bypass behaviour.
questions.remediation:
Review all active DLP policies in the Forcepoint Email Security/DLP console against the organisation's data classification policy and regulatory data protection requirements. Ensure that each DLP policy has a documented business requirement, designated owner, and defined review cycle. Engage data protection/compliance stakeholders in the policy review process.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DLP Policy Guide for policy design best practices. Engage Forcepoint Professional Services for a DLP policy alignment workshop if significant gaps are identified.

questions.text: Is sensitive data detection working correctly?
questions.description: If the DLP sensitive data detection engine is not correctly detecting the targeted data types (PII, PAN, PHI, intellectual property), the organisation has a false sense of protection while data loss events occur undetected. Incorrect classifier configuration, inadequate training data, or network connectivity issues can all cause silent detection failures.
questions.remediation:
Test sensitive data detection by sending test emails containing synthetic but realistic sensitive data (test credit card numbers, synthetic personal ID numbers, deliberately marked confidential documents). Verify that each test triggers the expected DLP policy action. Review the DLP detection rate and false positive rate in the reporting dashboard.

Forcepoint KB: 'Testing and validating DLP policies in Forcepoint Email Security' — refer to the Forcepoint DLP Administrator Guide > Policy Testing.

questions.description: DLP incidents that are generated but not reviewed represent wasted investment in detection capability. Unreviewed incidents may contain evidence of ongoing data exfiltration campaigns, insider threats, or compliance violations that escalate over time. Incident backlogs exceeding 24-48 hours indicate an understaffed or under-prioritised DLP response function.
questions.remediation:
Establish a DLP incident review workflow with defined SLAs (e.g., high-severity incidents reviewed within 4 hours, medium within 24 hours, low within 5 business days). Assign incident reviewers and ensure the team is trained on the review workflow. Configure incident escalation for high-severity events.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DLP Incident Management Guide for incident review workflow configuration.

questions.text: Is encryption enforced for sensitive emails?
questions.description: Without email encryption enforcement for sensitive communications, emails containing confidential data transmitted in plaintext can be intercepted in transit or at rest on recipient mail servers. Many regulatory frameworks explicitly require encryption for emails containing personal data, financial information, or health records.
questions.remediation:
Configure DLP-triggered email encryption in the Forcepoint Email Security gateway so that emails triggering specific DLP policies are automatically encrypted before transmission. Verify that the encryption service (S/MIME, TLS-enforced, or portal-based encryption) is correctly integrated and that encrypted email is successfully delivered to external recipients.

Forcepoint KB: 'Configuring email encryption in Forcepoint Email Security' — refer to the Administrator Guide > Encryption Integration.

questions.description: Email is a common channel for exfiltrating sensitive data via large attachments or bulk attachment sends. Without attachment restriction policies (size limits, specific file type restrictions for outbound), users can send arbitrarily large files or sensitive file types externally without control. This is both a data loss and a security risk.
questions.remediation:
Configure outbound attachment restrictions in the Forcepoint Email Security policy: set maximum attachment size limits, block outbound sending of high-risk file types (source code archives, database dumps, encrypted containers), and flag large attachment sends for review. Define a business exception process for legitimate bulk data transfers.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint Email Security Administrator Guide > Content Filtering > Attachment Management.

questions.description: If the user quarantine portal is inaccessible, users cannot review and release legitimate emails that have been incorrectly quarantined. This generates help desk tickets, delays business communications, and reduces trust in the email security system. An inaccessible quarantine is also a symptom of underlying service health issues.
questions.remediation:
Verify that the end-user quarantine portal URL is accessible from corporate endpoints and, where required, from external locations. Confirm that user authentication to the quarantine portal is functioning (integrated with Active Directory or LDAP). Send a test quarantine notification email and verify that the quarantine release link functions correctly.

Forcepoint KB: 'Configuring and troubleshooting the end-user quarantine in Forcepoint Email Security' — refer to the Administrator Guide > Quarantine Management > End-User Quarantine.

questions.description: Incorrectly configured quarantine policies — where the wrong type of email is quarantined, or where quarantine actions do not match organisational requirements — result in either excessive false positives burdening users and administrators, or insufficient quarantine causing malicious email to be delivered without a review step.
questions.remediation:
Review quarantine policy configuration in the Forcepoint Email Security console. Verify that quarantine actions are assigned to the appropriate message classifications (spam, suspected spam, malware, DLP violation). Confirm that the quarantine retention period is configured appropriately (typically 14-30 days for spam, shorter for malware).

Forcepoint KB: 'Quarantine policy configuration in Forcepoint Email Security' — refer to the Administrator Guide > Quarantine Management.

questions.description: A quarantine retention period that is too short causes users to miss the window for reviewing and releasing quarantined legitimate emails, leading to permanent email loss. A period that is too long causes excessive storage consumption and accumulates a large backlog of unreviewed quarantine entries.
questions.remediation:
Review the quarantine retention settings for each message category in the Forcepoint Email Security console. Set spam quarantine retention to 14 days minimum to allow users adequate time for review. Set malware quarantine retention to match the incident investigation timeline requirements. Confirm that quarantine storage capacity is sufficient for the configured retention period.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint Email Security Administrator Guide > Quarantine Configuration for retention period settings.

questions.text: Are users notified of quarantined emails?
questions.description: Without automated quarantine notifications, users are unaware that email addressed to them has been quarantined. This results in missed business communications, frustrated users who receive complaints from external senders about non-delivery, and increased reliance on administrator intervention to release legitimate email.
questions.remediation:
Configure quarantine digest notifications in the Forcepoint Email Security console to be sent to users on a defined schedule (daily or twice daily). Verify that notification emails include the quarantine release link, a preview of quarantined message subjects and senders, and instructions for reviewing the full quarantine portal. Test notification delivery to a test mailbox.

Forcepoint KB: 'Configuring quarantine notification emails in Forcepoint Email Security' — refer to the Administrator Guide > Quarantine Management > User Notifications.

questions.text: Is admin quarantine review performed regularly?
questions.description: The administrator quarantine — containing high-confidence spam, malware-suspected, and DLP-triggered messages — requires regular review by the security team. Unreviewed administrator quarantine accumulates false positives that block legitimate business communications and may contain evidence of ongoing attacks that is not being acted upon.
questions.remediation:
Establish a daily administrator quarantine review process. Assign responsibility for quarantine review to the email security operations team. Define criteria for releasing, deleting, or escalating quarantined messages. Configure administrator quarantine notifications to alert the team when high-severity messages are quarantined.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint Email Security Administrator Guide > Quarantine Management > Administrator Quarantine.

questions.description: Without documented quarantine release procedures, staff handling quarantine review may release messages inconsistently, inadvertently release malicious content, or be unable to handle quarantine management during the primary administrator's absence. Undocumented procedures also create audit and compliance gaps.
questions.remediation:
Document the quarantine release procedures including: criteria for release vs. deletion, the approval workflow for releasing high-severity quarantine items, steps for releasing messages to specific users, and the process for handling user release requests. Include procedures for handling quarantine during staff absence. Store documentation in the operations runbook.

Forcepoint KB: Engage Forcepoint Professional Services to review and validate quarantine management procedures as part of a Health Check engagement.

questions.text: Are email security reports generated regularly?
questions.description: Without regular email security reporting, the operations team lacks visibility into email threat trends, detection effectiveness, system health, and compliance metrics. Irregular reporting makes it impossible to identify emerging threats, justify security investments, or demonstrate compliance with regulatory reporting requirements.
questions.remediation:
Configure automated scheduled reports in the Forcepoint Email Security reporting console for: daily operational reports (message volumes, detection rates, quarantine stats), weekly threat trend reports, and monthly executive summaries. Ensure reports are delivered to the appropriate stakeholders. Review report content quarterly and adjust as required.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint Email Security Reporting Guide for scheduled report configuration.

questions.description: Management teams that do not receive regular executive summaries of email security performance lack the information needed to make informed decisions about security investments, policy changes, and risk acceptance. Without visibility, management may underestimate email-borne threat levels or overlook systemic issues identified in detailed operational reports.
questions.remediation:
Configure a monthly executive summary report summarising: total email volumes, spam/malware blocking rates, top threat categories, DLP incidents, system availability, and trend comparisons versus previous periods. Ensure the report is delivered to the CISO, IT Director, and other relevant management stakeholders. Translate technical metrics into business risk language.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint Email Security Reporting Guide > Executive Reporting.

questions.description: Without tracking email threat trends over time (increasing phishing attempts, new malware families, seasonal spam campaigns), the security team cannot proactively adjust controls before threat volumes peak. Reactive responses to trend changes result in increased malicious email reaching users during the adaptation period.
questions.remediation:
Configure trend tracking reports showing week-over-week and month-over-month comparisons for spam volume, malware detection, phishing attempts, and DLP incidents. Review trends weekly in the security operations meeting. Subscribe to Forcepoint Threat Intelligence reports and industry threat bulletins to contextualise observed trends.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint Email Security Reporting Guide > Trend Analysis. Integrate Forcepoint email threat intelligence feeds into the SIEM for correlation.

questions.description: Email security reporting data not retained for a sufficient period cannot support forensic investigations, regulatory audits, or retrospective security analysis. Compliance frameworks typically require reporting data retention aligned with the log retention period (minimum 1 year for most regulated environments).
questions.remediation:
Verify the reporting data retention configuration in the Forcepoint Email Security console. Ensure that reporting data is retained for at minimum 12 months, or longer if required by applicable regulations. Implement database archiving for older reporting data if storage constraints require it.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint Email Security Administrator Guide > Database Management for reporting data retention configuration.

questions.description: Without compliance-specific reports (GDPR data breach indicators, PCI-DSS email policy compliance, HIPAA PHI transmission tracking), the organisation cannot demonstrate to regulators or auditors that email security controls are functioning as required. Missing compliance reports create audit gaps and may result in regulatory findings.
questions.remediation:
Identify the compliance reporting requirements applicable to the organisation (GDPR, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, KVKK, ISO 27001). Configure email security reports that address each requirement: data breach indicator reports, DLP policy compliance reports, encryption usage reports. Ensure reports are generated on schedule and stored for the required retention period.

Forcepoint KB: Engage the Forcepoint compliance team or Professional Services for guidance on compliance-specific reporting.

questions.text: Is reporting integrated with security dashboard?
questions.description: Email security events not integrated into the security dashboard remain siloed and cannot be correlated with events from other security controls. SIEM integration enables threat correlation, automated response orchestration, and unified security visibility. Without integration, the SOC team must manually check a separate email security console for indicators of compromise.
questions.remediation:
Configure Forcepoint Email Security log forwarding to the SIEM platform via syslog or API integration. Verify that the SIEM is receiving and correctly parsing email security events. Create SIEM correlation rules that link email threat indicators (sender reputation, malicious links) with endpoint or network events.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint Email Security SIEM Integration Guide for log format specifications and integration configuration.

questions.text: Are custom reports configured for stakeholders?
questions.description: Generic reports may not provide the specific metrics required by specific stakeholders (IT helpdesk needing false positive data, compliance team needing DLP metrics, NOC needing system health data). Without stakeholder-specific custom reports, recipients receive reports containing largely irrelevant data and miss the specific metrics relevant to their role.
questions.remediation:
Conduct a stakeholder requirements review to identify what email security data each audience needs. Configure custom reports in the Forcepoint Email Security reporting console for each stakeholder group. Schedule reports at the appropriate frequency for each audience. Obtain feedback from stakeholders on report usefulness and adjust accordingly.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint Email Security Reporting Guide > Custom Report Configuration.

questions.text: Are DLP policies aligned with data classification?
questions.description: DLP policies that are not aligned with the organisation's data classification schema will either fail to protect classified data or generate excessive false positives that erode user and administrator trust. Misaligned policies are the most common cause of DLP programme underperformance and eventual abandonment.
questions.remediation:
Map all active DLP policies against the organisation's data classification levels (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted). For each classification level, verify that corresponding DLP policies exist, are enforced on appropriate channels, and that action severity matches the classification level. Involve data owners and the data protection officer in the policy alignment review.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DLP Policy Configuration Guide and the Forcepoint Data Classification Guide for policy alignment best practices. Engage Forcepoint Professional Services for a DLP policy review workshop.

questions.text: Is policy coverage comprehensive across channels?
questions.description: If DLP policy coverage is limited to only some channels (e.g., only email but not web or endpoint), sensitive data can be exfiltrated through unmonitored channels. Attackers and malicious insiders specifically target channels that they know are not monitored. Comprehensive channel coverage is a foundational DLP requirement.
questions.remediation:
Audit DLP policy coverage across all data channels: email (inbound/outbound), web/HTTP/HTTPS uploads, endpoint (USB, print, clipboard, cloud sync), network (FTP, SFTP), and cloud applications (CASB). Identify any channels where DLP policies are absent or where inspection is not occurring. Prioritise closing coverage gaps based on data exfiltration risk.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DLP Administrator Guide > Channel Coverage for channel-specific policy configuration.

questions.text: Are policy rules tested before enforcement?
questions.description: DLP policy rules deployed directly into enforcement mode without prior testing in monitor mode generate excessive false positives, block legitimate business workflows, and cause immediate user and business disruption. Untested policy rules are a common cause of DLP programme rejection by business stakeholders.
questions.remediation:
Implement a policy testing lifecycle: deploy new DLP rules in monitor (detection-only) mode for a minimum of 2 weeks before moving to enforcement. Analyse monitor mode results for false positive rates and tune rules before enforcement. Document test results and obtain business stakeholder sign-off before enabling blocking actions.

Forcepoint KB: 'DLP policy testing and tuning methodology for Forcepoint DLP' — refer to the Forcepoint DLP Administrator Guide > Policy Lifecycle Management.

questions.description: DLP policies that are not regularly reviewed become misaligned with changing business processes, regulatory requirements, and data classification schemas. Policies written for data types that no longer exist in the environment generate false positives, while new data types introduced by business changes may not be covered.
questions.remediation:
Establish a quarterly DLP policy review process. For each policy, verify that the targeted data types are still relevant, that detection accuracy is acceptable, and that channel coverage is complete. Involve data owners, legal, compliance, and security stakeholders in the review. Document review outcomes and changes in the policy change log.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DLP Policy Management Guide for policy lifecycle best practices.

questions.description: DLP false positives that are not actively addressed accumulate over time, creating an incident backlog that desensitises administrators, slows legitimate business workflows, and degrades trust in the DLP programme. High false positive rates indicate policy rules that need tuning.
questions.remediation:
Review the DLP incident queue and identify patterns of recurring false positives (same sender, same content type, same business context). Tune the relevant policy rules using exception lists, refined detection patterns, or source/destination whitelisting. Set a target false positive rate below 5% of total incidents. Track false positive rate as a monthly KPI.

Forcepoint KB: 'Tuning DLP detection accuracy and reducing false positives in Forcepoint DLP' — refer to the Forcepoint DLP Policy Tuning Guide.

questions.description: Without defined exception processes, business stakeholders who need to legitimately transfer sensitive data through channels that DLP policies would block have no formal path to obtain exceptions. This leads to shadow IT workarounds, conflict between security and business teams, and potential non-compliant data handling.
questions.remediation:
Define and publish a DLP exception process including: exception request form, approver hierarchy (data owner + security team), exception duration limits (typically 30-90 days), conditions under which exceptions are granted, and a register of all active exceptions. Implement exceptions in the Forcepoint DLP console using policy exclusions. Review the exception register quarterly.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DLP Administrator Guide > Policy Exceptions for technical implementation of exceptions.

questions.text: Are all endpoints reporting to the manager?
questions.description: Endpoints that are not reporting to the Forcepoint DLP manager have no DLP policy enforcement. Users on these endpoints can exfiltrate data via USB, print, clipboard, or cloud sync without any detection or blocking. Gaps in endpoint coverage are a critical DLP blind spot that is often exploited in insider threat scenarios.
questions.remediation:
Run the Forcepoint DLP endpoint coverage report to identify all endpoints that are not reporting (missing agents, offline machines, or agent failures). Investigate the cause for each category: deploy missing agents through the software distribution system, resolve agent errors, and flag chronic offline machines for investigation. Target 100% agent coverage with <5% offline at any given time.

Forcepoint KB: 'Forcepoint DLP Endpoint Agent deployment and management guide' — refer to the Administrator Guide > Endpoint Management.

questions.description: Running outdated versions of the Forcepoint DLP Endpoint Agent exposes the organisation to known agent vulnerabilities, policy enforcement gaps introduced in older versions, and compatibility issues with current operating system versions. Agents that are significantly behind the current version may silently fail to apply new policies.
questions.remediation:
Review endpoint agent versions across all managed endpoints using the Forcepoint DLP console endpoint inventory report. Identify endpoints running versions more than one major release behind the current version and prioritise their update. Deploy agent updates through the organisation's software distribution system (SCCM, Intune, Jamf) following the standard patch management process.

Forcepoint KB: 'Forcepoint DLP Endpoint Agent version management and upgrade guide' — refer to the Administrator Guide > Agent Lifecycle Management.

questions.text: Are offline endpoints identified and managed?
questions.description: Offline endpoints (laptops absent from the corporate network for extended periods) may have stale DLP policies applied and their policy violations are not reported to the DLP manager until they reconnect. Extended offline periods are a risk indicator — devices may have been lost, stolen, or intentionally taken offline to bypass monitoring.
questions.remediation:
Configure alerting in the Forcepoint DLP console for endpoints that have not connected for more than 7 days. Investigate offline endpoints: verify with the asset management team that the device is accounted for. For devices that reconnect after extended offline periods, review the violation log that syncs on reconnection. Escalate unusual offline patterns to the security team.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DLP Administrator Guide > Endpoint Offline Mode Management.

questions.text: Is endpoint coverage complete across organization?
questions.description: Incomplete endpoint coverage — where significant portions of the endpoint fleet do not have the DLP agent installed — creates systematic blind spots in the DLP programme. Unmanaged endpoints (BYOD, contractor machines, lab systems) are particularly high-risk as they are often used for work involving sensitive data.
questions.remediation:
Reconcile the Forcepoint DLP endpoint inventory with the authoritative asset management system (CMDB). Identify all endpoints in the CMDB that do not appear in the DLP endpoint inventory. Prioritise DLP agent deployment to endpoints with access to sensitive data stores. For BYOD and contractor endpoints, evaluate agentless DLP monitoring (proxy-based, CASB) as an alternative.

Forcepoint KB: 'Managing DLP coverage gaps and unmanaged endpoints in Forcepoint DLP' — refer to the Forcepoint DLP Deployment Guide.

questions.description: If endpoint DLP policies are not correctly deployed to managed endpoints — due to policy server communication errors, agent misconfigurations, or network connectivity issues — the endpoint is running without the intended policy set. This can result in data exfiltration that should have been blocked or detected by the policy.
questions.remediation:
Verify endpoint policy deployment status in the Forcepoint DLP console for each managed endpoint. Identify any endpoints showing policy deployment errors or stale policy versions. For endpoints with deployment failures, check agent logs (%ProgramData%\Forcepoint\DLP\logs) for error messages. Common causes include firewall blocking DLP manager communication and agent certificate issues.

Forcepoint KB: 'Troubleshooting DLP endpoint policy deployment failures in Forcepoint DLP' — refer to the Forcepoint DLP Endpoint Troubleshooting Guide.

questions.description: Without properly configured device control (USB, removable media, printer, Bluetooth, CD/DVD), users can exfiltrate data from managed endpoints through physical device channels that bypass network-based DLP controls. USB-based data theft is among the most common insider threat vectors in environments with unrestricted device access.
questions.remediation:
Review the device control policy configuration in the Forcepoint DLP console. Verify that USB storage is blocked or monitored with appropriate content scanning. Configure printer monitoring to capture print content for high-sensitivity documents. Evaluate Bluetooth, CD/DVD, and removable media restrictions based on the organisation's risk appetite. Create exceptions for authorised devices using hardware ID whitelisting.

Forcepoint KB: 'Configuring device control in Forcepoint DLP' — refer to the Administrator Guide > Endpoint > Device Control.

questions.description: Endpoint DLP incidents that are not reviewed may represent active data exfiltration, insider threats, or policy circumvention that escalates in scope over time. Unreviewed endpoint incidents are particularly serious because they often involve physical media and are difficult to trace retrospectively.
questions.remediation:
Establish a daily endpoint incident review process in the Forcepoint DLP incident management console. Configure incident routing so that high-severity endpoint violations (USB copy of classified files, large print jobs of sensitive documents) are immediately escalated to the security team. Track endpoint incident response SLAs and report compliance monthly.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DLP Incident Management Guide for endpoint incident review configuration.

questions.text: Is network DLP monitoring critical channels?
questions.description: If network DLP is not monitoring critical channels (SMTP, HTTP/HTTPS, FTP, cloud sync), sensitive data transmitted over those channels is invisible to the DLP programme. Network DLP provides the essential backstop for data exfiltration that bypasses endpoint controls (e.g., from unmanaged devices or through network-accessible applications).
questions.remediation:
Review the network DLP channel configuration in the Forcepoint DLP network sensor deployment. Verify that all critical channels are covered: SMTP (port 25), HTTPS (via SSL inspection), FTP/SFTP, web uploads (HTTP POST), and cloud sync protocols. Confirm that the network sensor has sufficient throughput capacity for the traffic volume on monitored segments.

Forcepoint KB: 'Forcepoint DLP network sensor deployment and channel coverage guide' — refer to the Forcepoint DLP Network Architecture Guide.

questions.description: Network DLP sensors positioned incorrectly in the network topology may miss traffic on certain segments, monitor encrypted traffic that cannot be decrypted, or be bypassed by traffic routed through alternative paths. Sensor positioning is critical for effective network DLP coverage.
questions.remediation:
Review the network DLP sensor deployment diagram against the current network topology. Verify that sensors are positioned to capture all egress traffic (at internet boundary, between security zones, and on cloud-connected segments). For HTTPS traffic, confirm that SSL inspection is configured upstream of the DLP sensor to provide plaintext content for inspection.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DLP Network Sensor Deployment Guide for sensor positioning best practices. Engage Forcepoint Professional Services for network architecture review if significant coverage gaps are identified.

questions.description: SMTP is the primary channel for email-based data exfiltration and is a mandatory coverage requirement for most regulatory frameworks. Without SMTP monitoring by the DLP sensor, sensitive data sent via email from non-gateway-managed mail clients or direct SMTP connections can bypass email gateway DLP controls.
questions.remediation:
Verify that the Forcepoint DLP network sensor is positioned to monitor SMTP traffic (port 25) on all segments through which corporate email traffic flows. Confirm that the sensor is decrypting SMTP over TLS (STARTTLS) where possible, or that the email gateway is integrated with DLP to provide TLS-decrypted message content.

Forcepoint KB: 'Configuring SMTP monitoring in Forcepoint DLP' — refer to the Network Sensor Configuration Guide. Confirm SMTP monitoring is active by generating a test email containing synthetic sensitive data and verifying incident generation.

questions.description: HTTP and HTTPS are the dominant channels for modern data exfiltration — through web-based file sharing, webmail, cloud storage uploads, and browser-based SaaS applications. Without HTTP/HTTPS inspection (which requires SSL decryption), the majority of modern data exfiltration activity is invisible to the DLP network sensor.
questions.remediation:
Verify that HTTP traffic inspection is active on the Forcepoint DLP network sensor. For HTTPS, confirm that SSL inspection is configured — either through integration with Forcepoint Web Security Content Gateway (which provides decrypted traffic to the DLP sensor) or through an independent SSL inspection appliance. Test HTTPS inspection by uploading a test file containing synthetic sensitive data to a cloud storage service.

Forcepoint KB: 'Configuring HTTP/HTTPS inspection in Forcepoint DLP with SSL decryption' — refer to the Forcepoint DLP + Web Security Integration Guide.

questions.description: File transfer protocols (FTP, SFTP, SCP, FTPS) remain active in many enterprise environments for batch data transfers and system integrations. Without DLP monitoring of these protocols, large-scale data exfiltration via file transfer is invisible. FTP is particularly risky as it transmits data in cleartext.
questions.remediation:
Review whether FTP, SFTP, and SCP traffic is present in the environment using network traffic analysis. Configure the Forcepoint DLP network sensor to monitor FTP traffic (port 21) and SFTP/SCP (port 22). For SFTP, note that content inspection of encrypted SFTP is not possible at the network layer — endpoint DLP controls are required for effective SFTP monitoring.

Forcepoint KB: 'Configuring file transfer protocol monitoring in Forcepoint DLP' — refer to the Network Sensor Configuration Guide.

questions.description: If network DLP performance is inadequate (high latency, packet drops, inspection timeouts), the system will either degrade user-facing network performance or be configured to bypass inspection for high-volume traffic. Both outcomes result in DLP coverage gaps. Network DLP sensors must be sized for the peak traffic volume on monitored segments.
questions.remediation:
Review the Forcepoint DLP network sensor performance metrics (CPU, memory, packet drop rate, inspection throughput). Compare against the rated throughput capacity of the sensor hardware/virtual machine. If the sensor is approaching capacity, evaluate traffic prioritisation (inspect high-risk protocols first) or add sensor capacity.

Forcepoint KB: 'Forcepoint DLP network sensor performance sizing guide' — refer to the Forcepoint DLP System Requirements. Engage Forcepoint Professional Services for sensor performance assessment.

questions.text: Are network policies synchronized with endpoints?
questions.description: Discrepancies between network DLP policies and endpoint DLP policies create coverage gaps where data types protected on the network are unprotected on endpoints, or vice versa. Policy inconsistencies are exploited by sophisticated insiders who know which channel is less strictly monitored.
questions.remediation:
Compare the active policy sets in the network DLP and endpoint DLP configurations. Identify any data types or channels where policies differ in scope or action. Establish a policy governance process that requires synchronised updates across network and endpoint policies when changes are made.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DLP Administrator Guide > Policy Management for cross-channel policy synchronisation guidance.

questions.text: Is cloud DLP configured for SaaS applications?
questions.description: Without cloud DLP configured for SaaS applications, sensitive data uploaded to or shared through sanctioned cloud apps (Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Salesforce, ServiceNow) is invisible to the DLP programme. Cloud adoption has made cloud-based data exfiltration the fastest-growing vector in the modern threat landscape.
questions.remediation:
Deploy Forcepoint DLP cloud channel coverage for all sanctioned SaaS applications in use. For Microsoft 365, integrate using the Microsoft Graph API or the Forcepoint ONE CASB connector. For other SaaS platforms, evaluate CASB-based API inspection or proxy-inline inspection. Prioritise coverage for cloud apps where sensitive data is known to reside.

Forcepoint KB: 'Configuring cloud DLP coverage for SaaS applications in Forcepoint DLP' — refer to the Forcepoint DLP Cloud Integration Guide and the Forcepoint ONE CASB documentation.

questions.description: Cloud storage platforms (SharePoint Online, OneDrive, Google Drive, Box, Dropbox) are the most common locations for sensitive data in modern enterprises and are also the most frequently exploited for data exfiltration and accidental exposure. Without DLP monitoring of cloud storage platforms, the majority of modern data at rest is unprotected.
questions.remediation:
Configure Forcepoint DLP or Forcepoint DSPM to scan all cloud storage platforms in use. For OneDrive/SharePoint Online, use the Microsoft Graph API integration. For Google Drive, use the Google Drive API integration. Configure data discovery scanning to identify sensitive data already at rest in cloud storage.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DLP Cloud Storage Integration Guide. Engage Forcepoint Professional Services for multi-cloud DLP deployment if more than three cloud storage platforms require coverage.

questions.text: Is API integration working with cloud apps?
questions.description: API integration failures between Forcepoint DLP and cloud applications result in blind spots where DLP policies are not being applied to cloud app traffic. API-based integration is the primary mechanism for cloud DLP enforcement in SaaS environments and its failure means the cloud channel is effectively unmonitored.
questions.remediation:
Test API connectivity between Forcepoint DLP and each configured cloud application by triggering a known test event (e.g., uploading a test file to a monitored cloud storage platform) and verifying incident generation. Check API credential validity and expiry for each integration. Review API call rate limits and verify that DLP inspection is not being throttled.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DLP Cloud Integration Guide for API troubleshooting. Monitor API integration health dashboards in the Forcepoint DLP console and configure alerting for API errors.

questions.text: Are cloud policies consistent with on-prem?
questions.description: Policy inconsistencies between cloud and on-premises DLP create double standards where the same sensitive data is protected in the corporate network but unprotected when moved to cloud services. This inconsistency is often exploited as a sanctioned workaround for moving data to less-monitored cloud environments.
questions.remediation:
Review and compare cloud DLP policies against the equivalent on-premises policies for each data type. Identify any gaps where on-premises policies exist but cloud equivalents have not been deployed. Establish a policy governance process that requires cloud policy updates to be synchronised with on-premises policy changes.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DLP Policy Management Guide for cross-environment policy consistency requirements.

questions.description: Without CASB integration, the organisation lacks visibility into which cloud applications are in use (shadow IT discovery), cannot enforce access policies for unauthorised cloud services, and cannot monitor user behaviour within sanctioned cloud applications. CASB is the primary control for cloud application DLP in modern enterprise environments.
questions.remediation:
Verify that Forcepoint CASB (or Forcepoint ONE) is integrated with the DLP platform for inline cloud traffic inspection. Confirm that cloud application policies are active and that shadow IT discovery is reporting newly identified unsanctioned applications. Review the cloud application risk assessment and take action on high-risk unsanctioned applications.

Forcepoint KB: 'Integrating Forcepoint CASB with Forcepoint DLP' — refer to the Forcepoint CASB Integration Guide. Note that DSPM and Classification proposals require mandatory Professional Services packages per Forcepoint go-to-market policy.

questions.text: Are cloud discovery findings being addressed?
questions.description: Cloud discovery findings (unsanctioned cloud applications, excessive data sharing, public access to sensitive repositories) that are not addressed accumulate into an unmanaged risk backlog. New risky cloud applications are adopted by business units continuously; unaddressed findings enable data exfiltration through unsanctioned channels.
questions.remediation:
Establish a cloud discovery finding review process with defined SLAs: high-risk findings (unsanctioned apps with sensitive data uploads) reviewed within 5 business days, medium-risk findings reviewed within 15 business days. Classify found cloud applications as sanctioned, tolerated, or blocked. Block high-risk unsanctioned applications in the proxy/CASB policy.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint CASB Administrator Guide > Shadow IT Discovery for finding management workflows.

questions.text: Is incident workflow defined and followed?
questions.description: Without a defined and followed incident workflow, DLP incidents are handled inconsistently — some reviewed, some ignored, different actions taken for similar violations. Inconsistent incident handling creates regulatory compliance gaps, allows repeated violations to continue unchecked, and makes it impossible to demonstrate a systematic data protection programme.
questions.remediation:
Define a written DLP incident response workflow covering: incident intake and triage, investigation steps, action options (warn, educate, escalate, block, report to HR/legal), documentation requirements, and closure criteria. Configure the workflow in the Forcepoint DLP incident management module. Train all DLP reviewers on the workflow.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DLP Incident Management Guide for workflow configuration. Integrate DLP incidents with the organisation's ITSM/ticketing system for SLA tracking.

questions.text: Are incidents being reviewed in timely manner?
questions.description: DLP incidents that are not reviewed in a timely manner allow data exfiltration to continue during the review delay. For high-severity incidents (classified data exfiltration, large volume data transfers), even a 24-hour review delay can mean significant additional data loss during the window between incident generation and investigation.
questions.remediation:
Define and enforce SLAs for DLP incident review based on severity: Critical (immediate block + review within 2 hours), High (review within 4 hours), Medium (review within 24 hours), Low (review within 5 business days). Configure automated escalation if incidents are not acknowledged within the SLA window.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DLP Incident Management Guide for SLA configuration and escalation rules.

questions.description: Without a defined incident escalation process, high-severity DLP incidents (data exfiltration by privileged users, mass download of classified files) may be handled at the wrong level — either under-escalated or inefficiently escalated without a clear path to decision makers for blocking or disciplinary action.
questions.remediation:
Define the DLP incident escalation matrix specifying: which severity levels require escalation, who is notified at each level (DLP analyst, security manager, CISO, HR, legal, business unit head), the timeline for escalation decisions, and the authority to take blocking or disciplinary action. Document the matrix in the DLP incident response procedure.

Forcepoint KB: Engage Forcepoint Professional Services to review and validate the incident escalation process as part of a DLP programme assessment.

questions.description: Without tracking incident metrics (total incidents, incidents by severity/channel/policy/user, false positive rate, resolution time), the DLP programme cannot demonstrate ROI, identify systemic policy problems, or report compliance to management and auditors. Untracked programmes lose funding and stakeholder support.
questions.remediation:
Configure monthly incident metric reports in the Forcepoint DLP reporting console. Track: total incidents by severity and channel, top violators, top violated policies, false positive rate, and review SLA compliance. Share metrics with the CISO and business unit heads monthly. Use trend data to justify policy improvements and programme investments.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DLP Reporting Guide for incident metric report configuration.

questions.text: Is incident data retained per policy?
questions.description: Incident data that is purged before the retention period required by the organisation's legal hold policy or regulatory framework cannot be used for litigation, regulatory investigations, or internal disciplinary proceedings. DLP incidents are often critical evidence in data breach investigations.
questions.remediation:
Review the Forcepoint DLP incident retention configuration and confirm it meets the organisation's requirements. Set retention to at minimum 1 year for all incidents, 3 years for high-severity incidents, or longer if required by applicable regulations. Implement archival of closed incidents to long-term storage before purge. Coordinate with legal on legal hold implications.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DLP Administrator Guide > Incident Data Retention. Align incident retention periods with the organisation's legal and compliance requirements.

questions.description: Repeat violations by the same users or involving the same data types/channels indicate that incident remediation (user warning, training) is not effective, or that policy configurations are generating sustained false positives for legitimate business activities. Unanalysed repeat incidents are a key indicator of DLP programme effectiveness gaps.
questions.remediation:
Configure the Forcepoint DLP reporting console to identify users with more than 3 incidents in a 30-day period. For repeat violators, escalate to HR or management for more formal intervention. For policies generating a high volume of repeat incidents from multiple users (potential false positives), review and tune the policy rule.
