Verify that the SSL inspection CA certificate is trusted by devices that initiate connections through the VPN. Monitor SSL inspection performance impact on VPN throughput.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint NGFW SMC Administrator Guide > VPN > SSL Inspection Integration for VPN-specific SSL inspection configuration.

questions.description: Without monitoring VPN performance metrics (throughput, latency, connection establishment time, active session count), the operations team has no visibility into whether VPN service quality is meeting user and business requirements. Unmonitored VPN performance degradation impacts remote worker productivity and may indicate capacity issues before they cause connection failures.
questions.remediation:
Configure VPN performance metric collection in the Forcepoint NGFW monitoring: track active session count, peak throughput, average connection latency, and authentication response time. Set alert thresholds for VPN performance degradation (response time >2 seconds, session count >80% of licensed capacity). Review VPN performance reports weekly. Include VPN performance in the monthly IT operations review.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint NGFW SMC Administrator Guide > VPN Monitoring > Performance Metrics for metric collection configuration.

questions.text: Are all cloud storage locations being scanned?
questions.description: If not all cloud storage locations are being scanned by Forcepoint DSPM, sensitive data residing in unscanned repositories is invisible to the data risk programme. Shadow data stores (unregistered S3 buckets, OneDrive sites created outside IT processes, Snowflake databases) are common blind spots that harbour the highest-risk data.
questions.remediation:
Review the Forcepoint DSPM cloud connector inventory and compare it against the organisation's authorised cloud infrastructure inventory (from cloud management platforms or CSPM tools). Identify any storage accounts, buckets, databases, or SaaS repositories that are not connected to DSPM. Prioritise connecting stores where sensitive data is expected to reside. Onboard all remaining stores within the agreed timeframe.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Cloud Connector Configuration Guide for supported cloud platforms (AWS S3, Azure Blob, OneDrive, GCP Storage, Snowflake, etc.). Note that DSPM proposals require mandatory Professional Services packages per Forcepoint go-to-market policy.

questions.description: Scanning frequency that is too low means that newly created sensitive data, changes in access permissions, or newly introduced compliance violations are not detected in a timely manner. A weekly or monthly scanning cycle may leave significant data exposure windows between scans, particularly in environments with high data creation and movement rates.
questions.remediation:
Review the scanning frequency configured in Forcepoint DSPM for each connected data store. For high-sensitivity stores (financial data, PII repositories, healthcare data), configure continuous or daily incremental scanning. For lower-sensitivity stores, weekly scanning may be acceptable. Ensure that on-demand scans can be triggered for newly onboarded data stores without waiting for the scheduled cycle.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Scan Schedule Configuration for scanning frequency options.

questions.description: In organisations using multiple cloud providers (AWS, Azure, GCP) or multiple SaaS platforms, gaps in multi-cloud DSPM coverage mean that sensitive data in non-covered environments is outside the data risk programme. Attackers increasingly target secondary or less-managed cloud environments precisely because they are less monitored.
questions.remediation:
Audit the DSPM connector inventory against the complete list of cloud platforms and SaaS services in use across the organisation. Identify any platforms without DSPM coverage. Engage Forcepoint Professional Services to deploy connectors for uncovered platforms. For platforms not yet supported by DSPM, document the gap and implement compensating controls (manual data discovery, CSPM scanning).

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Supported Platforms list on support.forcepoint.com for the current connector availability by cloud platform.

questions.description: Unacceptable scan performance — excessive scan duration, scan failures, or significant impact on production workload performance — causes scan schedules to slip, creating data discovery gaps. Performance issues also risk the organisation reducing scanning scope to compensate, permanently reducing coverage.
questions.remediation:
Review scan performance metrics in the Forcepoint DSPM console: average scan duration, scan success rate, and any performance impact alerts from scanned environments. For slow scans, evaluate whether incremental scanning is configured correctly. For scan failures, check connector health and cloud provider API rate limits. Engage Forcepoint Professional Services for scan performance optimisation.

Forcepoint KB: 'Optimising Forcepoint DSPM scan performance' — refer to the DSPM Administrator Guide > Scan Configuration and Performance.

questions.description: Scanning errors (failed scans, partial scans, connector authentication failures, API rate limit errors) result in data discovery gaps where sensitive data may not be identified. Unaddressed scanning errors can accumulate, causing entire data stores to go unscanned for extended periods without the operations team being aware.
questions.remediation:
Review the Forcepoint DSPM scan error log daily. Categorise errors by type (authentication failure, API rate limit, network timeout, unsupported data type) and assign remediation actions to each category. Configure alerting for scan errors so the operations team is immediately notified. Track scan error resolution SLAs and report on coverage gaps caused by errors.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Troubleshooting Guide for common scan error causes and resolution steps.

questions.description: Without incremental scanning configured, each scan cycle rescans all data from scratch, resulting in excessive API consumption, extended scan durations, and unnecessary load on cloud provider APIs. Full rescans on large data stores can take days, reducing the effective scanning frequency and creating data discovery gaps.
questions.remediation:
Enable incremental scanning in the Forcepoint DSPM scan configuration for each connected data store. Verify that the incremental scanning mechanism (change detection API, file modification timestamps, or event-based triggers) is correctly configured for each cloud platform. Monitor incremental scan durations versus full scan durations to confirm the performance improvement.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Scan Configuration > Incremental Scanning for platform-specific incremental scan configuration.

questions.description: Shadow IT cloud repositories (S3 buckets created by developers outside the IT process, OneDrive sites, Dropbox Business accounts) contain sensitive data that has never been assessed for data risk. Without shadow IT discovery, these repositories are invisible to the DSPM programme and represent an unmanaged data exfiltration risk.
questions.remediation:
Enable shadow IT repository discovery in Forcepoint DSPM or integrate with a CSPM/CASB tool to identify cloud resources not registered in the official cloud inventory. Review discovered shadow IT repositories weekly. For each discovered repository, engage the owner to either register it in the official inventory (and onboard it to DSPM) or decommission it. Block creation of unsanctioned cloud storage through cloud governance policies.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Shadow Data Discovery for shadow IT repository detection configuration.

questions.text: Is sensitive data discovery working correctly?
questions.description: If Forcepoint DSPM is not correctly discovering sensitive data across connected stores — due to misconfigured classifiers, missing data type patterns, or connectivity issues — the organisation has a false sense of data visibility. Critical sensitive data (PII, PAN, PHI, secrets) that is not discovered cannot be assessed for risk or protected.
questions.remediation:
Validate data discovery effectiveness by running test scans against data stores containing known synthetic sensitive data. Verify that all configured data types (PII, PAN, PHI, credentials, IP) are correctly detected. Compare DSPM discovery results against manual data samples from the same stores to identify missed detections. Review and update classifier configurations for any data types showing low detection accuracy.

Forcepoint KB: 'Validating sensitive data discovery accuracy in Forcepoint DSPM' — refer to the DSPM Administrator Guide > Data Discovery Validation.

questions.description: Inaccurate data classifiers in Forcepoint DSPM produce both false positives (non-sensitive data flagged as sensitive, causing unnecessary risk findings and remediation effort) and false negatives (sensitive data not detected, creating unmanaged risk). Classifier accuracy degrades over time if not periodically reviewed and retrained.
questions.remediation:
Review the detection accuracy of each DSPM classifier against a sample of manually reviewed data. For classifiers with false positive rates above 10% or false negative rates above 5%, tune the classifier pattern or confidence threshold. Submit misclassified data samples to Forcepoint for classifier improvement. Review classifier accuracy quarterly.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Classifier Configuration for classifier tuning procedures.

questions.description: Without PII detection configured in DSPM, the organisation cannot identify where personal data is stored across cloud environments, which is a fundamental requirement for GDPR, KVKK, PDPL, and other privacy regulations. Unknown PII locations cannot be protected, breach-notified, or subject to data subject rights requests.
questions.remediation:
Verify that PII detection classifiers are enabled in Forcepoint DSPM for all applicable regulatory frameworks (GDPR, KVKK, PDPL, CCPA). Confirm that the configured PII patterns include all relevant personal data types for the geographies in which the organisation operates (names, ID numbers, addresses, email addresses, phone numbers, biometric data). Test PII detection with synthetic data in test repositories.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Compliance Pack documentation for pre-built PII classifiers for major privacy regulations. Engage Forcepoint Professional Services for custom PII classifier development.

questions.description: Financial data (credit card numbers, bank account numbers, IBAN, SWIFT codes, financial reports) stored in cloud environments without DSPM detection creates PCI-DSS and financial regulatory compliance gaps. Financial data that is not identified cannot be scoped for PCI-DSS CDE controls or protected from unauthorised access.
questions.remediation:
Verify that financial data classifiers (PAN, IBAN, SWIFT, ABA routing numbers, bank account numbers) are enabled in Forcepoint DSPM. Confirm that financial data detection results are reviewed and that discovered financial data repositories are added to the PCI-DSS Cardholder Data Environment (CDE) scope. Test financial data detection with synthetic test patterns.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM PCI-DSS Compliance Pack for pre-built financial data classifiers.

questions.description: Health data (PHI - Protected Health Information) stored in cloud environments without DSPM detection creates HIPAA and local healthcare data privacy regulation compliance gaps. Healthcare organisations and their business associates are required to know where PHI is stored and to protect it accordingly.
questions.remediation:
Verify that PHI detection classifiers are enabled in Forcepoint DSPM for applicable healthcare data types (patient names, DOB, medical record numbers, diagnosis codes, prescription data, health insurance numbers). Confirm that discovered PHI repositories are assessed for HIPAA compliance controls and that access restrictions are verified.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM HIPAA Compliance Pack for pre-built PHI classifiers.

questions.description: Organisations with industry-specific sensitive data types (legal case references, engineering drawings, classified government data, proprietary financial models) that are not covered by standard DSPM classifiers will have significant detection gaps for their most valuable and sensitive intellectual property.
questions.remediation:
Identify the organisation's custom sensitive data types that are not covered by standard DSPM classifiers. Work with the Forcepoint DSPM team or Professional Services to develop custom classifiers using regular expressions, keyword lists, or machine learning models. Test custom classifiers against representative samples of the targeted data type before deployment.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Custom Classifier Development for custom classifier creation procedures.

questions.description: An unacceptable false positive rate in DSPM data discovery (non-sensitive data incorrectly classified as sensitive) generates excessive risk findings that overwhelm the security team, erode trust in the DSPM programme, and cause legitimate risk findings to be missed or deprioritised due to alert fatigue.
questions.remediation:
Review the false positive rate in Forcepoint DSPM findings by sampling a representative set of findings and manually validating whether the identified data is genuinely sensitive. For classifiers generating high false positive rates, adjust the confidence threshold or pattern specificity. Track the false positive rate as a monthly DSPM programme KPI and set a target rate below 15%.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Classifier Tuning for false positive reduction techniques.

questions.description: DSPM data discovery results that are not reviewed by a human analyst accumulate as unprocessed risk findings. Without regular review, high-priority findings (publicly accessible sensitive data, improperly shared confidential repositories) remain unaddressed, increasing the organisation's data breach risk over time.
questions.remediation:
Establish a weekly data discovery review process in the Forcepoint DSPM console. Assign a named reviewer responsible for reviewing new findings and assigning remediation tasks. Configure the DSPM dashboard to surface the highest-priority findings (most sensitive data type + highest access risk). Track the outstanding finding backlog size as a weekly KPI.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Findings Management for finding review and assignment workflows.

questions.description: Without a complete data inventory produced by DSPM scanning, the organisation cannot answer fundamental data governance questions: what sensitive data do we have, where is it stored, and who has access to it? An incomplete data inventory means that data protection, privacy rights fulfilment, and breach notification obligations cannot be fully met.
questions.remediation:
Verify that all cloud data stores in scope have been scanned at least once by Forcepoint DSPM and that the results are reflected in the data inventory. Identify any data stores not yet scanned and prioritise their onboarding. Review the data inventory completeness metrics in the DSPM dashboard and set a target of >95% of known data stores scanned within the past 30 days.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Data Inventory Management for inventory completeness tracking.

questions.description: Incorrect risk score calculations in Forcepoint DSPM — due to misconfigured risk scoring models, missing risk signals, or stale data — can cause high-risk findings to be deprioritised and low-risk findings to consume remediation capacity. Risk score accuracy is essential for effective resource allocation in data risk management.
questions.remediation:
Review the risk scoring configuration in Forcepoint DSPM and verify that all risk signals are correctly weighted: data sensitivity level, access breadth, public accessibility, regulatory impact, and data recency. Cross-reference a sample of DSPM-calculated risk scores against manual risk assessments to validate scoring accuracy. Adjust risk model parameters if significant discrepancies are found.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Risk Scoring Configuration for risk model customisation.

questions.description: Access risk — the risk posed by excessive user permissions, overly broad group memberships, and unnecessary service account access to sensitive data stores — is a primary driver of data breach impact. Without access risk evaluation in DSPM, sensitive data stores that are accessible to thousands of users may not be flagged as high-risk.
questions.remediation:
Verify that Forcepoint DSPM is connected to identity providers (Azure AD, Okta, AWS IAM) for access risk evaluation. Review the access risk findings in the DSPM console, focusing on data stores with sensitive classifications that are accessible by large groups or by users without a documented business need. Initiate access reviews and reduction for high-access-risk findings.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Access Risk Assessment for identity provider integration configuration.

questions.description: Publicly accessible data stores (S3 buckets with public-read ACL, SharePoint sites with anonymous access, Snowflake databases with public endpoints) that contain sensitive data represent the highest-priority data risk category. Publicly accessible sensitive data is frequently found by automated scanning tools used by threat actors and reported in external data breach notifications.
questions.remediation:
Review the Forcepoint DSPM findings filtered by 'public access' and 'sensitive data classification'. For each finding, immediately engage the cloud platform team to restrict public access. Configure cloud governance policies (AWS SCPs, Azure Policy, GCP Org Policy) to prevent future creation of publicly accessible storage resources. Track remediation progress daily until all public-access findings are resolved.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Public Access Risk Findings for prioritisation and remediation guidance.

questions.description: Sensitive data sharing risk — where sensitive data is shared externally with third parties, contractors, or other organisations without appropriate controls — creates data breach risk, contractual liability, and regulatory compliance gaps. Without DSPM assessment of data sharing practices, unknown external sharing of sensitive data may be ongoing.
questions.remediation:
Review the Forcepoint DSPM data sharing risk findings, focusing on sensitive data repositories with external sharing enabled. Identify all external parties with access to sensitive data and verify that each external access has a business justification, a data sharing agreement, and appropriate contractual data protection obligations. Revoke access for external parties that cannot be justified.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Data Sharing Risk Assessment.

questions.description: High-risk findings that are not prioritised for remediation remain as unaddressed security gaps. Without systematic prioritisation, the security team may focus on easily addressable low-risk findings while high-risk findings (publicly accessible PII, unencrypted PAN data) accumulate without remediation.
questions.remediation:
Configure the Forcepoint DSPM risk dashboard to display findings sorted by risk score, with the highest-risk findings (critical data type + public access + no encryption) at the top. Define a remediation SLA for each risk level: Critical findings remediated within 24 hours, High within 7 days, Medium within 30 days. Track SLA compliance and report deviations to management.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Risk Prioritisation for risk-based finding sorting and SLA configuration.

questions.description: Without risk trending data, the security team cannot determine whether the organisation's cloud data risk posture is improving or deteriorating over time. Risk trending is essential for demonstrating programme effectiveness to management, identifying emerging risk patterns, and justifying continued investment in data security.
questions.remediation:
Configure risk trending reports in Forcepoint DSPM to track: total risk score over time, number of findings by severity over time, remediation velocity (findings closed per period), and new findings introduced per period. Review risk trending data monthly in the security governance review. Use trend data to demonstrate DSPM programme ROI to management.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Risk Trending and Reporting for trend report configuration.

questions.description: Orphaned data — sensitive data in cloud stores belonging to former employees, decommissioned applications, or expired projects — represents unnecessary data risk. This data is often overlooked because it is not actively used, but it remains subject to breach notification requirements and access by current employees with broad storage permissions.
questions.remediation:
Enable orphaned data detection in Forcepoint DSPM by integrating with the HR system and application inventory to identify data stores owned by departed employees or decommissioned applications. Review orphaned data findings monthly. For confirmed orphaned data, initiate a data classification and deletion/archival process with the relevant data owner's manager.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Orphaned Data Detection and Management.

questions.description: Stale data — sensitive data that has not been accessed or modified for an extended period (e.g., more than 2 years) — may be retained beyond its business need, creating unnecessary compliance risk and storage costs. Data minimisation (a core principle of GDPR, KVKK, and PDPL) requires that personal data be deleted when no longer needed.
questions.remediation:
Configure stale data detection in Forcepoint DSPM based on last-accessed and last-modified timestamps. Review stale data findings to identify sensitive data repositories that have not been accessed for more than 12 months. Engage data owners to confirm whether the data is still required. Delete or archive confirmed stale data in accordance with the organisation's data retention policy.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Data Lifecycle Management for stale data detection and remediation.

questions.description: Without compliance policies configured in Forcepoint DSPM, the system scans and discovers sensitive data but does not evaluate findings against the specific requirements of applicable regulatory frameworks. This limits DSPM's usefulness for compliance reporting and means that regulatory violations in cloud data are not automatically surfaced.
questions.remediation:
Review the compliance policy configuration in Forcepoint DSPM and enable all applicable regulatory frameworks (GDPR, KVKK, PDPL, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001). For each enabled framework, verify that the associated data type classifiers and control requirements are correctly configured. Test compliance reporting by generating a compliance report and reviewing the findings against the framework requirements.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Compliance Pack documentation for pre-built compliance policies. Engage Forcepoint Professional Services to customise compliance policies for organisation-specific regulatory requirements.

questions.description: GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) compliance requires organisations to know where personal data is stored, ensure it is adequately protected, and respond to data subject rights requests. Without GDPR compliance monitoring in DSPM, the organisation cannot demonstrate compliance or respond effectively to regulatory enquiries and data breach notification obligations.
questions.remediation:
Enable the Forcepoint DSPM GDPR compliance policy and verify that all GDPR-relevant personal data types (names, email addresses, ID numbers, financial data, health data) are included in the detection configuration. Review the GDPR compliance findings and prioritise remediation for personal data stores that are inadequately protected, publicly accessible, or retained beyond their stated purpose.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM GDPR Compliance Pack. Engage the organisation's DPO in the GDPR compliance finding review and remediation prioritisation.

questions.description: For organisations operating in or serving patients in the United States, HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act) requires specific controls for PHI (Protected Health Information). Without HIPAA compliance tracking in DSPM, PHI in cloud environments may not meet HIPAA's Security Rule requirements for access controls, encryption, and audit logging.
questions.remediation:
Enable the Forcepoint DSPM HIPAA compliance policy if the organisation is a covered entity or business associate. Verify that PHI detection classifiers are correctly configured. Review HIPAA compliance findings to identify PHI stores that are not encrypted at rest, have excessive access, or lack audit logging. Implement remediation for each finding in alignment with HIPAA Security Rule requirements.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM HIPAA Compliance Pack for pre-built HIPAA compliance policy configuration.

questions.description: For organisations that process payment card data, PCI-DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard) requires that cardholder data stored in cloud environments is scoped, protected, and subject to specific security controls. Without PCI-DSS compliance verification in DSPM, cardholder data in cloud stores may be outside the formally declared CDE scope.
questions.remediation:
Enable the Forcepoint DSPM PCI-DSS compliance policy. Verify that financial data classifiers (PAN, CVV, expiry date) are correctly detecting cardholder data across all connected cloud stores. Review PCI-DSS compliance findings and ensure that all discovered cardholder data stores are added to the CDE scope and subject to appropriate PCI-DSS controls (encryption, access control, audit logging).

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM PCI-DSS Compliance Pack for pre-built PCI-DSS policy configuration.

questions.description: Data residency compliance requirements (GDPR Article 44, KVKK cross-border transfer restrictions, Saudi Arabia NCA requirements, UAE PDPL) mandate that certain categories of personal data must remain within specified geographic boundaries. Without data residency compliance checks in DSPM, sensitive data may be inadvertently stored in non-compliant cloud regions.
questions.remediation:
Enable data residency compliance checks in Forcepoint DSPM for all applicable regulatory frameworks. Configure the allowed and prohibited cloud regions for each data type and regulatory requirement. Review data residency compliance findings and immediately remediate any sensitive data found in prohibited regions by migrating it to a compliant region or deleting it.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Data Residency Compliance for region restriction configuration. Engage the organisation's legal and compliance team to define data residency requirements for each applicable regulation.

questions.description: Without automated compliance report generation, demonstrating regulatory compliance to auditors, regulators, and executive management requires time-consuming manual data collection from the DSPM console. Manual compliance reporting is prone to errors, delays, and inconsistencies that undermine the credibility of the compliance programme.
questions.remediation:
Configure scheduled compliance report generation in Forcepoint DSPM for each applicable regulatory framework. Schedule monthly compliance reports and quarterly executive summary reports. Automate report delivery to the compliance team, CISO, and DPO. Retain compliance reports for the period required by each regulatory framework.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Reporting Guide for compliance report configuration and scheduling.

questions.description: Without a maintained audit trail, it is impossible to demonstrate to regulators that data protection controls have been consistently applied, that access to sensitive data has been properly controlled, and that data breaches have been handled in accordance with notification obligations. Audit trail integrity is a fundamental requirement of all major data privacy regulations.
questions.remediation:
Verify that Forcepoint DSPM maintains a comprehensive audit trail of all system events: scans performed, findings generated, access reviews completed, remediation actions taken, and policy changes made. Confirm that the audit trail is immutable (cannot be modified or deleted by standard users). Forward DSPM audit events to the SIEM for long-term retention and correlation.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Audit Trail Configuration for audit log configuration.

questions.description: Compliance violations discovered by DSPM that are not remediated represent ongoing regulatory non-compliance. Unaddressed violations compound over time — a single GDPR violation that is not remediated may become a pattern of violations that significantly increases regulatory penalty exposure.
questions.remediation:
Review all open compliance violations in the Forcepoint DSPM compliance dashboard. Prioritise violations by regulatory impact (data subject rights violations, breach notification obligations, cross-border transfer violations). Assign each violation a remediation owner and SLA. Track remediation progress in a governance dashboard. Report outstanding violations to the DPO and CISO weekly.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Compliance Management Guide for violation tracking and remediation workflow configuration.

questions.description: Without automated remediation configured for high-confidence, low-risk remediation actions (e.g., removing public access from a bucket containing sensitive data), DSPM findings accumulate into a manual remediation backlog that grows faster than the security team can address. Automated remediation for well-defined, safe actions dramatically reduces the time from discovery to protection.
questions.remediation:
Identify DSPM finding categories that are safe to remediate automatically without human review: removing public access from storage buckets, revoking expired service account access, adding encryption to unencrypted stores. Configure Forcepoint DSPM automated remediation policies for these categories. Ensure automated remediation actions are logged in the audit trail and send notification emails to data owners.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Automated Remediation Configuration for supported automated actions.

questions.description: Without defined remediation workflows, security team members handle DSPM findings ad-hoc, with inconsistent processes, variable response times, and no systematic tracking. Undefined workflows also make it impossible to report remediation performance metrics or demonstrate a structured data protection programme to auditors.
questions.remediation:
Define and document DSPM remediation workflows for each finding category: who is notified, what information they receive, what action is required, the SLA for completion, and the escalation path for missed SLAs. Integrate DSPM findings into the organisation's ticketing system (Jira, ServiceNow) to enable systematic tracking and SLA enforcement.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Remediation Workflow Configuration for ticketing system integration options.

questions.text: Is access revocation automated when needed?
questions.description: Without automated access revocation for data stores where excessive access is discovered, DSPM findings about over-permissioned access accumulate without remediation. Manual access revocation processes are slow, error-prone, and struggle to keep pace with the continuous creation of new access permissions in cloud environments.
questions.remediation:
Configure Forcepoint DSPM to automatically trigger access review or revocation workflows when excessive access to sensitive data is discovered. Integrate with identity governance tools (Saviynt, SailPoint, or cloud IAM) to automate access reviews. For automated revocation of high-risk access (e.g., public access), ensure that revocation policies are tested in non-production before enabling automation in production.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Access Risk Remediation for automated access workflow configuration.

questions.text: Are data owners notified of issues?
questions.description: Without automated notifications to data owners when sensitive data issues are discovered in their data stores, the people best positioned to make informed remediation decisions are not engaged in the process. Security-team-only remediation of data ownership issues creates bottlenecks and fails to build a data-ownership culture in the organisation.
questions.remediation:
Configure Forcepoint DSPM to automatically notify data owners (as identified through the cloud resource tagging or identity directory) when new findings are created for data stores they own. Notification emails should include: the finding summary, the risk score, the specific data types affected, and the action required. Include escalation contacts for cases where the data owner is unavailable.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Data Owner Notification Configuration.

questions.description: Without remediation tracking in place, open findings accumulate without visibility into whether remediation is progressing. Untracked remediation creates a situation where the same findings are discovered repeatedly across scan cycles without being resolved, generating false assurance about the data risk posture.
questions.remediation:
Enable remediation tracking in Forcepoint DSPM or integrate with the organisation's ticketing system to create, assign, and track remediation tasks for each finding. Configure the DSPM dashboard to display outstanding remediation tasks by age, severity, and owner. Generate weekly remediation progress reports for the security governance team.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Remediation Tracking and Ticketing Integration.

questions.description: Without SLAs defined for remediation of DSPM findings, there is no accountability mechanism for ensuring findings are addressed within a timeframe appropriate to their risk level. Undefined SLAs inevitably result in the highest-risk findings remaining open indefinitely while lower-effort findings are closed first.
questions.remediation:
Define remediation SLAs for each DSPM finding severity level: Critical (publicly accessible PII/PAN) — 24 hours; High (sensitive data with excessive access) — 7 days; Medium (sensitive data with suboptimal security) — 30 days; Low (informational) — 90 days. Configure SLA tracking in the DSPM console or the integrated ticketing system. Report SLA compliance to the CISO monthly.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > SLA Configuration for finding SLA setup.

questions.description: Sensitive data that has exceeded its retention period and is no longer required for business purposes should be deleted or archived in accordance with the organisation's data retention policy. Without automated deletion or archival processes, retained data that is no longer needed continues to accumulate risk and creates data minimisation compliance gaps.
questions.remediation:
Configure Forcepoint DSPM to flag data that has exceeded its configured retention period for each data type and regulatory framework. Implement an automated workflow that notifies data owners and schedules deletion or archival for overdue data. Integrate with cloud lifecycle management policies (S3 lifecycle rules, Azure lifecycle management) to automate archival to cold storage.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Data Lifecycle Automation for deletion and archival workflow configuration.

questions.description: Without remediation reports, management cannot assess whether the DSPM programme is reducing data risk over time or whether the security team is effectively addressing findings. Unreported programme performance erodes management support and makes it difficult to justify continued investment in data security tooling.
questions.remediation:
Configure monthly remediation performance reports in Forcepoint DSPM covering: total findings opened and closed in the period, average time to remediation by severity, SLA compliance rate, and trends in outstanding finding backlog. Present remediation reports to the CISO and security governance committee monthly. Use report data to justify staffing, tooling, and process investment.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Reporting Guide > Remediation Performance Reporting for report configuration.

questions.description: Without Forcepoint DLP integration, DSPM findings about sensitive data locations cannot automatically trigger DLP policy updates to protect newly discovered sensitive data stores. The two tools operating independently creates a gap between discovery (DSPM) and enforcement (DLP) that leaves sensitive data unprotected between discovery and manual policy update.
questions.remediation:
Configure the Forcepoint DSPM to DLP integration to automatically create or update DLP policies when new sensitive data stores are discovered. Verify that DLP policies are applied to cloud data channels monitored by DSPM. Test integration by discovering synthetic sensitive data in a test environment and verifying that a corresponding DLP policy is created.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM + DLP Integration Guide for integration configuration. Note that DSPM proposals require mandatory Professional Services packages per Forcepoint go-to-market policy.

questions.description: Without SIEM integration, DSPM security events (new public-access findings, compliance violations, high-risk data discoveries) are siloed in the DSPM console and cannot be correlated with events from other security controls or trigger automated response workflows. SIEM integration is essential for incorporating DSPM into the security operations workflow.
questions.remediation:
Configure Forcepoint DSPM to forward security events to the SIEM platform via syslog or API integration. Create SIEM detection rules for high-priority DSPM events: new publicly accessible sensitive data discovered, compliance violation generated, high-risk finding created. Integrate DSPM findings into the SOC daily operations dashboard.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM SIEM Integration Guide for event forwarding configuration and event format specifications.

questions.description: Without ticketing system integration, DSPM remediation tasks are managed within the DSPM console, creating a separate workflow from the security team's primary work management system. Siloed task management reduces visibility, makes SLA tracking difficult, and causes findings to be missed when team members don't regularly log into the DSPM console.
questions.remediation:
Integrate Forcepoint DSPM with the organisation's ticketing system (Jira, ServiceNow, Azure DevOps) to automatically create tickets for new DSPM findings requiring remediation. Configure ticket fields to include: finding severity, data type, cloud resource, risk score, remediation owner, and SLA due date. Verify ticket synchronisation (status updates in the ticketing system should be reflected in DSPM).

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Ticketing Integration for supported ticketing system connectors.

questions.description: Forcepoint DSPM uses cloud provider APIs and potentially SaaS platform APIs to perform data scanning. API access credentials (IAM roles, service account keys, OAuth tokens) that are not properly secured can be compromised and used to exfiltrate the sensitive data that DSPM is supposed to protect. Insecure DSPM API access is a significant security risk in itself.
questions.remediation:
Review the API credentials used by Forcepoint DSPM for each cloud platform connector. Verify that: service accounts use the minimum permissions required for scanning (read-only where possible), credentials are stored in a secrets management solution (AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, HashiCorp Vault), credentials are rotated regularly (at minimum every 90 days), and access is restricted to the DSPM platform IP addresses.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Connector Security for API credential management best practices.

questions.description: Cloud provider APIs (AWS S3 API, Azure Storage API, Microsoft Graph API, Snowflake API) that are not properly connected to Forcepoint DSPM result in those cloud platforms not being scanned. API connection failures may occur silently — the DSPM connector may show as configured but not actively scanning if the API connection has expired or been revoked.
questions.remediation:
Test each cloud provider API connection in the Forcepoint DSPM connector configuration by running a test scan against a known data store. Verify that API credentials are current and have not expired. Check for API rate limiting warnings that may indicate the connection is not functioning at full capacity. Configure alerting for connector authentication failures.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Connector Health Monitoring for API connection testing procedures.

questions.description: Without identity provider integration in Forcepoint DSPM, the system cannot evaluate access risk against actual user and group memberships. Access risk assessments that don't account for who has access to sensitive data are incomplete — a data store may appear low-risk based on its sensitivity classification but be extremely high-risk if thousands of users have read access to it.
questions.remediation:
Configure Forcepoint DSPM identity provider integration for all applicable identity providers (Azure AD/Entra ID, Okta, AWS IAM, GCP IAM). Verify that user and group membership data is being synchronised correctly. Review access risk findings that are now enriched with identity context and prioritise remediation for sensitive data stores accessible by large groups or by users outside the expected user population.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DSPM Administrator Guide > Identity Provider Integration for supported IdP connectors and configuration procedures.

questions.text: Is the AI classification engine trained properly?
questions.description: An AI classification engine that has not been properly trained on the organisation's specific data types, document formats, and language characteristics will produce inaccurate classifications across all documents. Improperly trained models generate high false positive and false negative rates that undermine the entire classification programme.
questions.remediation:
Review the training data used for the Forcepoint Data Classification AI engine. Verify that training data is representative of the organisation's document types, languages, and sensitive content patterns. Evaluate the model's performance against a held-out test set of manually classified documents. If accuracy is below acceptable thresholds (typically >85%), engage Forcepoint Professional Services for model retraining with additional training data.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint Data Classification (FDC) Administrator Guide > AI Engine Configuration for training data requirements. Note that FDC proposals require mandatory Professional Services packages per Forcepoint go-to-market policy.

questions.text: Are classification models up to date?
questions.description: Classification models that are not updated over time fail to accurately classify new document types, newly adopted file formats, or emerging sensitive data patterns. As the organisation's data landscape evolves (new business units, new product types, regulatory changes), classification models must be updated to maintain accuracy.
questions.remediation:
Establish a quarterly classification model review process. Evaluate the model's accuracy against new document samples collected since the last update. Identify any document types or content patterns where classification accuracy has declined. Submit new training samples to Forcepoint for model updates. Review model version release notes from Forcepoint for available improvements.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC Administrator Guide > Model Update Management for model update procedures.

questions.description: Machine learning classification accuracy below acceptable thresholds (typically 85% correct classification rate) means that a significant proportion of documents are being incorrectly classified — either assigned the wrong classification level or not classified at all. Low accuracy undermines the usefulness of classification for DLP policy enforcement and user decision-making.
questions.remediation:
Measure the current ML classification accuracy by running the engine against a test set of 100-200 manually classified documents representative of the organisation's document corpus. Calculate precision (correctly classified as sensitive / total classified as sensitive) and recall (correctly classified as sensitive / total actually sensitive). If either metric is below 85%, initiate a model improvement process with additional training data.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC Administrator Guide > Classification Accuracy Measurement for accuracy measurement methodology.

questions.description: Classification false positives (documents classified at a higher sensitivity level than warranted) cause user friction, workflow disruption, and DLP policy blocks on legitimate activities. Persistent false positives erode user trust in the classification system and often result in users overriding classification suggestions, defeating the purpose of automatic classification.
questions.remediation:
Configure a false positive reporting mechanism in the Forcepoint FDC console that allows users to flag incorrect classifications. Review reported false positives weekly and use them to identify patterns (specific document types, authors, or content structures that are consistently misclassified). Submit false positive samples to Forcepoint for model tuning. Track the false positive rate as a monthly KPI.

Forcepoint KB: 'Managing and reducing classification false positives in Forcepoint Data Classification' — refer to the FDC Administrator Guide > False Positive Management.

questions.description: Without scheduled model retraining, classification accuracy gradually degrades as the organisation's data landscape evolves. New document types, new business terminology, and changes in sensitive data patterns are not reflected in the model, causing accuracy to decline over time without any visible trigger event.
questions.remediation:
Schedule quarterly model retraining sessions using accumulated new training data (correctly classified documents, reviewed false positives, new document types). Document the retraining schedule and the training data used in each retraining cycle. Test the retrained model against a held-out test set before deploying to production. Compare accuracy metrics to the previous model version.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC Administrator Guide > Model Retraining Schedule for retraining configuration and procedures.

questions.description: Standard classification models may not accurately identify the organisation's proprietary data types (specific product names, internal project code names, legal references, proprietary financial metrics). Without custom classifiers for these organisation-specific data types, the classification programme will miss a potentially significant category of sensitive intellectual property.
questions.remediation:
Identify the organisation's proprietary sensitive data types that are not captured by standard Forcepoint FDC classifiers. Work with department heads and the data protection officer to document these data types with examples. Develop custom classifiers using keyword lists, regular expressions, or ML training data for each proprietary data type. Test custom classifier accuracy against sample documents.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC Administrator Guide > Custom Classifier Development for custom classifier creation procedures.

questions.description: Without monitoring AI engine performance metrics (throughput, response time, CPU/memory usage, error rate), the operations team has no visibility into whether the classification engine is functioning correctly or whether performance degradation is affecting user-facing classification experience. Silent engine performance issues reduce classification coverage.
questions.remediation:
Configure performance monitoring for the Forcepoint FDC AI engine: track documents processed per hour, average classification response time, engine error rate, and system resource utilisation. Set alert thresholds for performance degradation (response time >5 seconds for interactive classification, throughput below expected baseline). Review performance metrics weekly and address any degradation trends.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC Administrator Guide > Engine Performance Monitoring for available metrics and monitoring configuration.

questions.description: Confidence threshold settings in the classification engine determine when the engine applies a classification automatically versus when it presents it as a suggestion to the user. Thresholds that are set too low cause over-confident incorrect classifications, while thresholds set too high cause the engine to default to user prompts too frequently, increasing classification burden on users.
questions.remediation:
Review the confidence threshold configuration for each classification level in the Forcepoint FDC engine. Compare the threshold values against the measured precision/recall at each threshold level. Adjust thresholds to optimise for the acceptable false positive/false negative balance for each classification level. Document the rationale for each threshold setting.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC Administrator Guide > Confidence Threshold Configuration for threshold tuning guidance.

questions.description: If automatic classification is not working — due to agent failures, engine connectivity issues, policy server errors, or unsupported file types — users are presented with empty classification prompts or classification is skipped entirely. Without automatic classification suggestions, the burden of correct classification falls entirely on untrained users, resulting in widespread misclassification.
questions.remediation:
Test automatic classification by opening and saving documents of each key type (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, PDF, email) from a managed endpoint. Verify that the FDC agent presents classification suggestions automatically based on content analysis. Check FDC agent logs on the endpoint for any connection errors to the classification engine. Verify that the classification engine service is running and reachable from endpoints.

Forcepoint KB: 'Troubleshooting automatic classification in Forcepoint Data Classification' — refer to the FDC Agent Troubleshooting Guide.

questions.text: Are classification labels aligned with organizational policy?
questions.description: Classification labels that do not align with the organisation's official data classification policy confuse users, make policy compliance impossible, and render the classification system unusable for regulatory reporting. Label misalignment commonly occurs when the IT team implements the classification system before the data classification policy is finalised.
questions.remediation:
Review all configured classification labels in Forcepoint FDC against the organisation's officially approved data classification policy. Verify that label names, definitions, and associated handling requirements match the policy document. For any discrepancies, update the FDC label configuration to match the approved policy. Obtain sign-off from the data protection officer on the label configuration.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC Administrator Guide > Label Configuration for label management procedures.

questions.description: A label taxonomy that is not clearly defined — with ambiguous label names, overlapping definitions between adjacent classification levels, or labels that don't map to real data handling requirements — causes systematic misclassification by users who cannot determine the correct label for their content. Ambiguous taxonomies are a primary cause of classification programme failure.
questions.remediation:
Review the label taxonomy for clarity and disambiguation. For each classification level, define: the label name, a concise definition (1-2 sentences), 3-5 examples of content that belongs at this level, and 3-5 examples of content that should NOT be at this level (to clarify boundaries with adjacent levels). Publish the taxonomy with worked examples in the organisation's data handling policy and user training materials.

Forcepoint KB: Engage Forcepoint Professional Services to review and improve the classification label taxonomy. Refer to industry classification frameworks (e.g., UK Government Security Classification) for taxonomy design best practices.

questions.description: Classification labels that are not visible to users in the applications where they work (Office suite, email client, PDF viewer, web browsers) do not influence user behaviour and cannot be used to make informed decisions about data handling. Label visibility in applications is fundamental to user-driven classification.
questions.remediation:
Verify that Forcepoint FDC label markings are displayed in all applications commonly used to create and consume classified data: Microsoft Office documents (header/footer/watermark markings), emails (subject line/body prefix), PDFs, and SharePoint/Teams. Test label visibility across all application versions and platforms (desktop, web, mobile) in use in the organisation.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC Administrator Guide > Label Visualisation Configuration for application-specific marking configuration.

questions.description: Without manual labelling enabled, users cannot override incorrect automatic classifications or add classifications to document types that the automatic engine cannot process (e.g., unusual file formats, legacy document types, physical document scan outputs). Manual labelling is an essential complement to automatic classification.
questions.remediation:
Verify that manual labelling is enabled in the Forcepoint FDC configuration and that the label selection interface is available in all supported applications. Configure the FDC policy to allow users to select labels from the full taxonomy (not a restricted subset). Ensure that the label application interface is accessible and discoverable by non-technical users.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC Administrator Guide > Manual Labelling Configuration for UI configuration.

questions.description: Without default labels configured for common document creation scenarios (new document creation, email composition, file save without explicit classification), users are required to actively select a classification label for every document and email. The additional friction causes users to skip classification, resulting in large volumes of unclassified documents.
questions.remediation:
Configure sensible default labels in the Forcepoint FDC policy for different document creation contexts: new document creation in office applications, new email composition, and file save events for specific application types. Set the default to the appropriate label for the majority of the organisation's documents (typically 'Internal' or 'Confidential' for corporate environments). Allow users to override the default upward or downward based on actual content sensitivity.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC Administrator Guide > Default Label Configuration for context-specific default label setup.

questions.description: Without label inheritance working correctly, classification labels are not propagated from parent documents to derivative works (copies, extracts, summaries, email attachments). A classified document that is copied and pasted into a new document may lose its classification, creating a gap where derivative sensitive content is unclassified.
questions.remediation:
Test label inheritance behaviour in the Forcepoint FDC deployment: copy content from a classified document and paste it into a new document, then verify that the new document receives at least the same classification level as the source. Attach a classified document to an email and verify that the email is classified at least at the same level as the attached document. Review FDC inheritance policy settings for each supported application.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC Administrator Guide > Label Inheritance Configuration for inheritance rule setup.

questions.description: Without configured label colours and icons, all classification labels appear visually identical in the application interface, making it difficult for users to quickly identify the classification level of a document at a glance. Visual differentiation (colour coding, icons) is a recognised best practice for improving classification awareness and reducing user error.
questions.remediation:
Configure distinctive visual representations for each classification level in Forcepoint FDC: assign a colour associated with risk level (e.g., green for Public, yellow for Internal, orange for Confidential, red for Restricted), and configure icons or badges that appear in the document header and application taskbar. Test visual representations across all supported applications and screen configurations.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC Administrator Guide > Label Visual Configuration for colour and icon assignment.

questions.text: Is label downgrade prevented or controlled?
questions.description: Without controls preventing label downgrade, users can reclassify sensitive documents to lower classification levels to bypass DLP restrictions, share data more broadly, or reduce document handling requirements. Unauthorised label downgrading is a common technique for insider data exfiltration.
questions.remediation:
Configure the Forcepoint FDC policy to require administrator approval or multi-person approval for label downgrade operations (e.g., reducing from Restricted to Confidential). Log all label downgrade events in the audit trail. Configure SIEM alerting for high-volume or unusual label downgrade patterns. Review label downgrade logs monthly as part of the insider threat monitoring programme.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC Administrator Guide > Label Downgrade Controls for downgrade restriction configuration.

questions.description: Without mandatory labelling policies enforced, users can create, save, and share documents without ever applying a classification label. Unclassified documents are excluded from label-based DLP enforcement, creating systematic gaps in data protection for all content that users have not proactively classified.
questions.remediation:
Configure Forcepoint FDC mandatory labelling policies that require users to apply a classification label before a document can be saved or sent. Implement application-level enforcement in Microsoft Office and email clients. For file system-level enforcement, configure FDC to prompt for classification when unlabelled files are detected. Set a target of <5% of new documents without a classification label within 90 days of deployment.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC Administrator Guide > Mandatory Labelling Policy Configuration for enforcement setup.

questions.text: Is DLP policy enforcement based on labels?
questions.description: Without DLP policy enforcement based on classification labels, the DLP system cannot protect classified documents using the most reliable signal available — the data owner's or AI engine's classification decision. Label-based DLP enforcement eliminates the need for content-based detection for labelled documents and significantly reduces false positive rates.
questions.remediation:
Configure Forcepoint DLP policies to use Forcepoint FDC classification labels as primary policy triggers. For each classification level (Confidential, Restricted), define DLP policy actions appropriate to the label (e.g., Confidential = monitor, block upload to unapproved cloud; Restricted = block all external sharing, require encryption). Test label-based DLP enforcement by attempting to share a document labelled at each classification level through various channels.

Forcepoint KB: 'Integrating Forcepoint Data Classification labels with Forcepoint DLP policies' — refer to the Forcepoint DLP + FDC Integration Guide.

questions.text: Are classified documents monitored by DLP?
questions.description: Without DLP monitoring of classified documents, classification labels are applied but do not trigger any protective action when classified documents are shared inappropriately. Classification without DLP enforcement is awareness-only — it informs users but does not enforce data handling rules when users choose to ignore them.
questions.remediation:
Verify that Forcepoint DLP is configured to monitor and enforce policies for documents bearing Forcepoint FDC classification labels. Confirm that monitoring is active across all channels: email, web/HTTP, endpoint (USB, print), and cloud upload. Test DLP detection of classified documents by attempting to share a test document bearing a high-classification label through various channels.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DLP Administrator Guide > Label-Based Policy Configuration.

questions.description: Without label-based blocking configured, the DLP system can detect inappropriate sharing of classified documents but cannot prevent it in real time. Detection-only (monitor mode) for classified data means that data exfiltration of classified documents occurs before the security team can respond.
questions.remediation:
Configure Forcepoint DLP blocking policies for classified documents being shared through unauthorised channels: block outbound email attachment of Restricted documents to external recipients, block upload of Confidential documents to unapproved cloud storage, block USB copy of Restricted documents. Implement blocking in stages starting with the highest-classification level to manage false positive impact.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DLP Administrator Guide > Label-Based Blocking Policy Configuration.

questions.text: Are DLP incidents correlated with labels?
questions.description: Without correlating DLP incidents with classification labels, it is impossible to determine which classification levels are generating the most violations, which users are mishandling classified content, and whether specific classification levels require more restrictive DLP policies. Uncorrelated incidents cannot drive label-specific policy improvements.
questions.remediation:
Configure Forcepoint DLP incident reports to include the classification label associated with each incident. Create label-specific incident dashboards showing incident counts, top violators, and top violated channels for each classification level. Use label-level incident data to identify which classification levels require policy tightening or user training interventions.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DLP Reporting Guide > Label-Based Incident Reporting for label correlation report configuration.

questions.text: Is classification data sent to DLP system?
questions.description: Without classification label data being sent to the DLP system, the DLP engine cannot enforce label-based policies. Integration data flow failures (FDC to DLP metadata transfer) cause the DLP system to operate without classification label context, reverting to content-pattern-only detection and missing the accuracy benefits of label-based enforcement.
questions.remediation:
Verify the data flow between Forcepoint FDC and Forcepoint DLP by confirming that label metadata is being correctly embedded in documents (via file properties or metadata fields) and that the DLP engine is reading and correctly interpreting the label data. Test integration by labelling a test document and confirming that the DLP engine generates an incident based on the label when the document is shared.

Forcepoint KB: 'Troubleshooting Forcepoint FDC to DLP label metadata transfer' — refer to the Forcepoint FDC + DLP Integration Guide > Troubleshooting.

questions.text: Are label changes triggering DLP re-evaluation?
questions.description: If label changes (upgrades or downgrades) do not trigger DLP policy re-evaluation, documents may be enforced under the DLP policy for their original label rather than their current label. A document upgraded from Confidential to Restricted should immediately be subject to more restrictive DLP controls — without re-evaluation, it continues to be enforced at the Confidential level.
questions.remediation:
Verify that Forcepoint DLP is configured to monitor label change events from Forcepoint FDC and to re-evaluate applicable DLP policies when a document's label changes. Test label change re-evaluation by upgrading a test document's label from Confidential to Restricted and confirming that the DLP blocking policy for Restricted label is immediately applied to subsequent operations on the document.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC + DLP Integration Guide > Label Change Re-evaluation for configuration requirements.

questions.text: Is automated remediation based on labels?
questions.description: Without automated remediation based on classification labels (e.g., automatically encrypting newly labelled Restricted documents, automatically removing external sharing when a document is upgraded to Confidential), the classification programme creates awareness of risk but does not reduce it automatically. Manual remediation for label-triggered findings scales poorly.
questions.remediation:
Configure automated remediation actions in Forcepoint DLP triggered by classification labels: encrypt all documents labelled Restricted when saved to shared storage, revoke external sharing links when a document is upgraded to Confidential, move documents labelled Restricted from public to private repositories. Test each automated remediation action with a test document before enabling in production.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint DLP Administrator Guide > Label-Based Automated Remediation for supported automated actions.

questions.description: Users who are not trained on data classification cannot correctly classify documents, apply labels appropriately, or understand the data handling requirements associated with different classification levels. Undertrained users are the primary cause of misclassification errors in enterprise classification programmes.
questions.remediation:
Develop and deliver a data classification awareness training programme covering: the classification schema and label definitions, how to apply labels in Microsoft Office and email, how to handle documents at each classification level, consequences of misclassification, and how to seek help. Deliver initial training to all employees before or concurrent with FDC agent deployment. Require annual refresher training.

Forcepoint KB: Engage the Forcepoint training team or Professional Services for user awareness programme development. Integrate classification training into the organisation's security awareness programme.

questions.text: Is training material available and current?
questions.description: Without current, accessible training material, users who forget their initial training have no reference to consult when classification decisions are unclear. Outdated training material that does not reflect the current classification taxonomy or data handling policy creates confusion and misclassification.
questions.remediation:
Maintain a current classification training resource library including: the classification policy document, label definition reference card (with examples), how-to guides for each supported application, FAQs for common classification scenarios, and a short video overview. Review and update training materials whenever the classification schema or data handling policy changes. Publish materials on the intranet and link from the FDC label application interface where supported.

Forcepoint KB: Engage Forcepoint Professional Services for training material development as part of the FDC implementation project.

questions.description: Without published classification guidelines, users interpret the classification schema subjectively, leading to inconsistent classification decisions across teams, departments, and geographies. Inconsistency undermines the reliability of classification as a signal for DLP enforcement and regulatory reporting.
questions.remediation:
Publish clear, specific classification guidelines for each label level with worked examples from real document types common in the organisation. Include classification decision trees for common ambiguous scenarios (e.g., 'an email containing both public and confidential information should be classified as....'). Publish guidelines in a location accessible from within the FDC label application interface. Review guidelines annually.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC Administrator Guide > User Guidance Configuration for embedding guidance in the label application interface.

questions.description: Without measuring user adoption of the classification system, the organisation cannot determine whether the classification programme is achieving its objectives or whether intervention is needed to drive adoption. Low adoption rates allow large volumes of unclassified content to accumulate outside the DLP enforcement perimeter.
questions.remediation:
Configure adoption metrics reporting in Forcepoint FDC: track the percentage of new documents created with a classification label, the distribution of labels applied (to identify misuse of the default label), and the rate of user-initiated classification vs. automatic classification. Review adoption metrics monthly. Target >95% of new documents classified within 90 days of programme rollout.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC Reporting Guide for user adoption metrics configuration.

questions.description: Without classification examples provided to users, the label definitions remain abstract and difficult to apply to real-world documents. Users faced with classification decisions they find unclear will default to the lowest-effort option (the default label or no label), resulting in systematic underclassification of sensitive content.
questions.remediation:
Develop a classification examples library for each label level with 5-10 real or realistic anonymised examples of documents that belong at that level. Include examples of borderline cases (documents that could be either Confidential or Restricted) and explain the deciding factors. Publish examples in the training material and embed links in the FDC label application interface.

Forcepoint KB: Engage Forcepoint Professional Services for examples development as part of the FDC user adoption programme.

questions.text: Is help desk trained on classification questions?
questions.description: Without helpdesk staff trained on classification questions, users who need guidance on how to classify specific documents have no effective support channel. Unanswered classification questions result in users making uninformed decisions, often defaulting to lower classification levels to avoid the stricter data handling requirements associated with higher levels.
questions.remediation:
Include a classification-specific training module in the IT helpdesk onboarding programme. Provide helpdesk staff with the classification guidelines, a decision tree for common classification questions, and an escalation path to the data protection team for ambiguous cases. Create a classification FAQ document based on the most common helpdesk enquiries about classification.

Forcepoint KB: Engage Forcepoint Professional Services for helpdesk training development as part of the FDC implementation project.

questions.description: Without scheduled refresher trainings, users' awareness of classification requirements degrades over time. New employees who missed the initial training rollout have no formal mechanism to receive classification training. Programme changes (new labels, updated data handling requirements) may not reach all users without regular training cycles.
questions.remediation:
Schedule annual refresher classification training for all employees. Create a condensed refresher format (15-30 minutes) focusing on programme updates since the last training cycle, common misclassification patterns identified through incident analysis, and any regulatory developments that affect data handling requirements. Require completion tracking to identify employees who have not completed refresher training.

Forcepoint KB: Integrate classification refresher training into the organisation's annual security awareness programme using the existing LMS platform.

questions.description: Without collecting user feedback on the classification system, the classification programme team has no channel to identify usability issues, points of friction that reduce adoption, or classification scenarios that users find confusing. Unresolved usability issues accumulate and contribute to declining adoption rates over time.
questions.remediation:
Implement a feedback mechanism for the classification system: a short in-application feedback prompt, an email alias for classification feedback, or periodic user surveys. Review collected feedback monthly and categorise by type (training gap, policy ambiguity, technical issue, workflow friction). Use feedback data to prioritise training updates, policy clarifications, and technical improvements.

Forcepoint KB: Engage Forcepoint Professional Services to review user feedback and recommend programme improvements as part of an annual FDC health check.

questions.description: Without classification reports generated regularly, the programme team lacks the operational visibility needed to manage the programme effectively. Unreported classification activity means that systematic misclassification patterns, adoption gaps, and label distribution anomalies go undetected until they cause significant problems.
questions.remediation:
Configure scheduled classification reports in the Forcepoint FDC reporting console: daily operational reports (label application activity, agent health), weekly adoption reports (% documents classified, label distribution), and monthly executive reports (programme KPIs, trend analysis). Review reports in the security operations meeting. Escalate significant anomalies (e.g., sudden drop in adoption rate) to the classification programme owner.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC Reporting Guide for scheduled report configuration.

questions.description: Without tracking label usage metrics, the classification programme team cannot identify whether users are using the correct labels for their content type, whether specific teams are systematically over- or underclassifying, or whether the label distribution is consistent with what would be expected for the organisation's data profile.
questions.remediation:
Configure label usage tracking in Forcepoint FDC to report: total documents labelled by level, label application by department/user, label change frequency, and the ratio of automatic to manual classifications. Review label usage trends quarterly. Investigate anomalous patterns (e.g., a specific team classifying everything as Public) to identify training gaps or policy misunderstandings.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC Reporting Guide > Label Usage Reports for usage metric configuration.

questions.description: Without monitoring classification trends over time, the programme team cannot identify gradual degradation in classification quality (e.g., a slow increase in misclassification events, a decline in adoption rate after initial enthusiasm), which could indicate model drift, training gaps, or policy confusion that requires intervention.
questions.remediation:
Configure classification trend reports in Forcepoint FDC covering: month-over-month changes in adoption rate, misclassification incident rate trends, label upgrade/downgrade event trends, and AI engine accuracy trends. Review trend data quarterly in the classification programme review meeting. Investigate any negative trends (declining adoption, increasing misclassification) with root cause analysis.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC Reporting Guide > Trend Analysis for trend reporting configuration.

questions.text: Is reporting data exported to analytics?
questions.description: Without exporting classification reporting data to analytics platforms, the classification programme cannot be integrated into the organisation's broader security and governance reporting ecosystem. Siloed classification data cannot be correlated with DLP incidents, data risk findings, or HR data for insider threat analysis.
questions.remediation:
Configure Forcepoint FDC to export reporting data to the organisation's analytics platform (Power BI, Tableau, Splunk) via API or data export. Create integrated security dashboards that combine classification metrics with DLP incident data, DSPM findings, and access control data. Use integrated analytics to identify correlations between classification adoption and DLP incident rates.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC API documentation for reporting data export capabilities.

questions.description: Without compliance reports available from the classification system, the organisation cannot use classification data as evidence of data protection programme effectiveness for regulatory audits or compliance certifications. Classification compliance evidence is increasingly required by regulators as part of demonstrating a systematic approach to data protection.
questions.remediation:
Configure compliance-specific reports in Forcepoint FDC that demonstrate: the percentage of sensitive data stores with classified content, the consistency of classification label application across regulated data types, and the integration of classification with DLP enforcement.
