Map report metrics to the requirements of applicable regulatory frameworks (GDPR Article 24, ISO 27001 Annex A.8.2).

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC Compliance Reporting Guide for compliance report configuration.

questions.description: Without an executive dashboard configured for the classification programme, senior leadership lacks the high-level visibility needed to support, fund, and champion the classification programme. Executive-level sponsorship is essential for classification programme success; sponsors without data to demonstrate progress tend to reduce or withdraw support.
questions.remediation:
Configure an executive classification dashboard in Forcepoint FDC or the organisation's BI platform showing: classification adoption rate (% new documents classified), label distribution across the organisation, DLP incident rate reduction attributable to classification, and compliance status metrics. Update the dashboard weekly and present in monthly security governance meetings.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC Reporting Guide > Executive Dashboard Configuration for dashboard setup.

questions.description: Without tracking misclassification incidents, the organisation cannot identify which users, teams, or document types are generating the highest rates of incorrect classification. Untracked misclassification is a leading indicator of user training gaps, policy ambiguity, and AI engine accuracy issues that require targeted intervention.
questions.remediation:
Configure misclassification incident tracking in Forcepoint FDC by correlating user-submitted false positive reports, helpdesk reclassification requests, and automated misclassification detection (where the AI engine's classification confidence contradicts the user-applied label). Produce monthly misclassification incident reports broken down by department, label level, and document type.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC Administrator Guide > Misclassification Tracking for incident tracking configuration.

questions.text: Is ROI of classification being measured?
questions.description: Without measuring the ROI of the classification programme, the security team cannot justify the ongoing investment in Forcepoint FDC licensing, Professional Services, and operational overhead. Programme leadership without ROI data is vulnerable to cost-reduction initiatives that eliminate the classification programme before it achieves its full risk reduction potential.
questions.remediation:
Define and track ROI metrics for the classification programme: reduction in DLP false positive rates attributable to label-based enforcement, reduction in data breach investigation time (classification labels speed up forensic triage), reduction in user reclassification requests (indicating improved classification accuracy), and compliance audit efficiency gains. Report ROI metrics to the CISO and IT Director quarterly.

Forcepoint KB: Engage Forcepoint Professional Services for ROI measurement framework development as part of the annual FDC programme review.

questions.description: Without audit reports generated from the classification system, the organisation cannot demonstrate to internal auditors or external regulators that the classification programme has been operating consistently and as designed. Audit reports are required evidence for ISO 27001 certification, PCI-DSS compliance, and GDPR Article 24 compliance.
questions.remediation:
Configure automated audit report generation in Forcepoint FDC covering: all label application events (who applied what label to which document, when), all label change events (upgrades and downgrades with approver information), policy changes, and administrator access events. Generate quarterly audit reports and retain them for the period required by applicable regulatory frameworks.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC Administrator Guide > Audit Report Configuration for audit report setup.

questions.description: Without data coverage reporting showing the percentage of the organisation's data estate that has been classified, the programme team cannot quantify the scope of classified vs. unclassified data. Unknown classification coverage means that the DLP enforcement perimeter based on labels is unknown in scope, creating hidden data protection gaps.
questions.remediation:
Configure data coverage reporting in Forcepoint FDC to show: the total volume of documents in the monitored data estate (from agent telemetry and DSPM integration), the percentage that have a classification label, and the distribution of unclassified documents by location, owner, and file type. Set a target of >90% of sensitive documents classified within 12 months of programme rollout.

Forcepoint KB: Refer to the Forcepoint FDC Reporting Guide > Data Coverage Reporting for coverage metric configuration.
